description:
Location:
Navi Mumbai, MH, IN, 400708
Requisition ID: 19473
About Holcim
As the world’s global leader in innovative and sustainable building materials, Holcim is reinventing the way the world builds. Supported by a 45,000-strong global team spread across 44 countries and four industry segments (Cement, Aggregates, Ready-Mix Concrete and Solutions & Products), we are committed to shaping a greener, smarter and healthier world. It’s our ambition to lead the industry in reducing carbon emissions and accelerating the transition towards low-carbon constructions globally.
About The Role
We are seeking an experienced Sourcing & Procurement Manager to lead end to end sourcing and procurement on all aspects of our India Business services Centre and Digital Hub (main categories include but not limited to IT, Facility, Infrastructure & Other Indirect category). In this role, you will lead sourcing, commercial negotiations, drive end-to-end category strategy, and partner closely with internal business stakeholders, Compliance, and Legal teams and vendors. You will be responsible for initiating, executing, and closing high-value procurement ensuring contracts while safeguarding the organization against legal, reputational, and compliance risks.
The ideal candidate will combine strong commercial negotiation skills with expertise in regulatory compliance (sanctions screening, anti-bribery & corruption directives), contract management, foundational working understanding of SAP PR/PO/Invoices workflows and practicing AI for automation
Key Requirements
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering (MBA or PGDM preferred).
• Experience: 8+ years of core experience in Strategic Sourcing, Commercial Negotiations, and Contract Management for India, APAC & EU 
• In depth knowledge of Anti-Bribery & Corruption (ABC) policies, and knowledge of sanctions screening & vendor due diligence tools.
• Strong working knowledge of SAP PR/PO process flows and P2P lifecycles.
• Familiarity with Indian tax structures (GST, TDS) and local commercial statutory compliance.
• Strong communication, negotiation, and cross-functional stakeholder management capabilities.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Negotiations
• Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across IT and Indirect categories, with a strong focus on IT procurement, Contract Staffing, Facility, HR & Consulting Services. 
• Execute commercial negotiations to optimize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), secure competitive pricing structures, and obtain favorable commercial & payment terms.
• Lead competitive bidding including RFPs, RFQs, and market benchmarking to select lowest cost , high performing suppliers.
Contract Management
• Partner directly with the Legal team to initiate, draft, negotiate, and finalize contracts, including Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), SLAs, and Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
• Proactively identify and mitigate contractual, commercial, and operational risks by enforcing essential clauses (indemnity, liability, data privacy, termination rights, and penalties).
• Manage contract renewals, amendments, and vendor obligations to ensure full compliance.
Compliance & Sanctions Screening
• Sanctions & Third-Party Screening: Conduct comprehensive due diligence and mandatory sanction screening on all new and existing vendors prior to onboarding.
• Statutory Compliance: Ensure strict adherence to Indian/EU legal frameworks, local procurement laws, GST mandates, TDS/WHT applicability, and internal compliance guidelines.
• Maintain complete audit trail readiness for internal and external regulatory audits.
SAP Workflow Management
• Understanding the entire P2P cycle with strong hands-on experience of Purchase Requisitions (PR) and Purchase Order (PO) creation and approval workflows in SAP. Must know Invoice/SES workflows
• Coordinate with internal procurement operations and finance teams to ensure POs align accurately with executed contracts and commercial terms.
Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) & Stakeholder Management
• Oversee vendor performance evaluations through periodic scorecards, key performance metrics, and Annual Business Reviews
• Build collaborative relationships with cross-functional business heads to align sourcing strategies with business budgets and project timelines.
• Serve as the single point of contact to resolve vendor performance issues, commercial disputes, and contract ambiguities.
Nice to Have
• Professional certification in procurement (e.g. CPSM, CIPS, or CSCP).
• Exposure to modern e-Sourcing platforms (e.g. SAP Ariba, Coupa, or Fair Markit).
• AI-Based Sourcing & Automation: Exposure to or familiarity with AI-driven procurement tools, Hands on expertise with ChatGPT, Gemini and automation platforms

title: Strategic Sourcing Manager
description:
Global Procurement Category Manager – Capital Projects (CapEx)
This position reports to the Global Procurement Category Lead – Capital Projects within a centralized procurement organization. The primary responsibility is to develop and lead global sourcing strategies for given set of CapEx categories in the space of equipment, construction, and engineering services.
This role involves developing sourcing strategies, managing key contracts, leading complex sourcing initiatives, and collaborating closely with internal stakeholders and suppliers to ensure capital are delivered efficiently, within budget, and aligned with overall business objectives. The ideal candidate will leverage market insights, data analysis, and strong negotiation skills to drive value, optimize total cost of ownership (TCO), and ensure compliance with procurement policies. CapEx procurement experience in the space of Electrical, Instrumentation & Automation and general contractor will be preferred.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Category Strategy & Execution
• Lead development and implementation of CapEx category strategies in alignment with global sourcing objectives.
• Conduct market analysis, benchmarking, and supplier evaluations to identify sourcing opportunities and drive cost competitiveness.
• Manage / support end-to-end sourcing processes for equipment and construction/engineering services, from RFQ to negotiation and contract award.
• Ensure adherence to category strategies and procurement governance across all projects.
• Monitor category performance and identify opportunities for value creation and continuous improvement.
2. Procurement Operations
• Lead sourcing events for assigned CapEx projects in close coordination with project teams and engineering functions.
• Negotiate commercial and contractual terms with suppliers to optimize total cost of ownership (TCO) while ensuring quality and delivery commitments.
• Coordinate supplier qualification, technical bid evaluations, and risk assessments.
• Support contract drafting, execution, and lifecycle management in collaboration with Legal and other internal partners.
• Drive Best-Cost Country Sourcing (BCCS) initiatives where applicable.
3. Project & Stakeholder Management

title: Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing Core/Agile 1
description:
We Are Teva
We’re Teva, a leading innovative biopharmaceutical company, enabled by a world-class generics business. Whether it’s innovating in the fields of neuroscience and immunology or delivering high-quality medicine worldwide, we’re dedicated to addressing patients’ needs now and in the future. Here, you will be part of a high-performing, inclusive culture that values fresh thinking and collaboration. You'll have the room to grow, the flexibility to balance life with work, and the opportunity to better health worldwide, together.
The Opportunity
The Senior Manager – Strategic Sourcing ‘Core/Agile’ is responsible for leading and executing strategic sourcing and contracting activities across assigned External Manufacturing (EXM) Core/Agile portfolio areas, aligned to priorities set by Procurement Category Management, Teva’s Core/Agile EXM organizations and Teva’s Core/Agile Manufacturing organization. This role plays a key part in delivering sourcing strategies, executing sourcing events, and driving measurable value through disciplined sourcing practices.
Reporting to the Senior Director – Strategic Sourcing Core / Agile Lead, this role operates as a hands-on sourcing manager, operationalizing category strategies and business requirements into RFx events, negotiations, and contracts. The Senior Manager is accountable for driving sourcing execution excellence, ensuring consistency in approach, and building strong working relationships with stakeholders and suppliers.
This role is well suited for a sourcing professional who is comfortable owning execution, leading sourcing initiatives, and driving results in a developing procurement environment.
How You’ll Spend Your Day
Strategic Sourcing Execution
• Lead end-to-end strategic sourcing events for assigned EXM categories, suppliers, or initiatives in alignment with established category strategies and sourcing priorities.
• Plan and execute RFx events, negotiations, and supplier selections with appropriate guidance from the Senior Director.
• Capture category strategies into clear execution plans, timelines, and deliverables.
• Ensure sourcing activities address cost, capacity, quality, service, and risk considerations.
Contracting & Commercial Support
• Lead commercial negotiations with suppliers, including pricing, capacity, and key commercial terms.
• Partner with Legal and cross-functional teams to support contract development, review, and execution using established templates.
• Support contract implementation by ensuring clarity of sourcing intent and negotiated outcomes.
• Identify and escalate commercial or contractual risks as appropriate.
Value Delivery & Tracking
• Deliver measurable sourcing value through cost optimization, negotiations, and contract execution aligned to category strategy objectives.
• Support achievement of annual savings and value targets; clearly articulate sourcing approach and outcomes to stakeholders.
• Track sourcing activities, outcomes, and benefits using standard tools and templates.
• Support Finance with value validation and reporting processes.
Supplier Engagement & Market Insight
• Engage suppliers through structured sourcing processes and commercial discussions.
• Maintain awareness of supplier capabilities, capacity constraints, and relevant market dynamics, including should cost analysis and supplier economics.
• Provide market and supplier insights to Category Managers and leadership to support planning and execution.
• Support resolution of sourcing-related supplier issues within contractual scope.
Risk, Compliance & Quality Alignment
• Ensure sourcing activities comply with procurement policies, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.
• Identify and escalate sourcing-related risks (e.g., capacity, single sourcing, commercial exposure).
• Collaborate with Quality, Regulatory, and Manufacturing teams to ensure sourcing decisions are feasible and compliant.
• Utilize procurement systems and tools effectively to support sourcing execution and tracking.
Stakeholder Partnership
• Partner with Category Managers, External Manufacturing, Quality, and Other stakeholders to execute sourcing initiatives.
• Communicate sourcing plans, progress, and outcomes clearly and consistently.
• Build credibility through reliable delivery and effective collaboration.
Process & Capability Development
• Apply standard sourcing tools, templates, and ways of working consistently.
• Identify opportunities to improve sourcing efficiency and execution discipline within assigned scope.
• Contribute to development and refinement of sourcing playbooks and standard work.
• Support adoption of procurement systems and tools as capabilities mature.
Your Qualification And Experience
EDUCATION
• Master’s degree with 8 + years of overall experience and 4 + years of relevant pharmaceutical direct / contract manufacturing sourcing and procurement experience
• Full-time MBAs preferred , especially from leading institutions.
Expertise
• Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end strategic sourcing and contracting activities, preferably within External Manufacturing or regulated industries.
• Strong working knowledge of sourcing and negotiation practices.
• Experience delivering savings and sourcing value initiatives.
• Familiarity with pharmaceutical, biotech, or regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
Skills & Attributes
• Strong execution and delivery mindset with attention to detail.
• Effective negotiation and commercial acumen.
• Solid stakeholder communication and collaboration skills.
• Analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
• Ability to operate effectively in evolving procurement environments
Experience Leading Sourcing Initiatives Or Projects Required.
How We’ll Take Care of You
At Teva India, care is at the heart of how we work. From your first day, you’ll be welcomed into a people-first culture built on inclusion, respect, and belonging.
That support extends to you and your loved ones through benefits designed for real life. These include comprehensive medical insurance, OPD coverage, annual health checkups, term life and accident insurance, and confidential emotional wellbeing support through our Optum Employee Assistance Program. You’ll also enjoy healthy meals at work, holistic wellbeing initiatives, and volunteering programs that help you give back to the community.
Your growth matters too. You’ll have opportunities to build future-ready skills, collaborate on projects with global teams, explore internal career opportunities, and learn through programs such as our AI-enabled Teva Twist program, R&D Academy, continuing education, and mentorship.
Join our vibrant workplace, where we celebrate milestones, festivals, achievements, and community impact together.
Teva’s Equal Employment Opportunity Commitment
Teva Pharmaceuticals is committed to equal opportunity in employment. It is Teva's global policy that equal employment opportunity be provided without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, disability, pregnancy, medical condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, ancestry, veteran status, national or ethnic origin or any other legally recognized status entitled to protection under applicable laws. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace for all. If you are contacted for a job opportunity, please advise us of any accommodations needed to support you throughout the recruitment and selection process. All accommodation information provided will be treated as confidential and used only for the purpose of providing an accessible candidate experience.

Education, Behaviors, Competencies, Skills:

Behavioral

• Shapes strategy upstream through close business partnership
• Deliver total enterprise value beyond savings
• Takes ownership of spend and outcomes end to end
• Uses curiosity, insights, and data to drive better decisions
These principles define how we partner with the business, our suppliers, and each other. Role-specific examples of these behaviors are embedded throughout the objectives, accountability, and skills outlined in this job description.
Competencies and skills 
• 10 + years of experience in category management, strategic sourcing, procurement, or related commercial functions within complex global and matrixed organizations
• Proven experience developing and executing category strategies that deliver sustainable enterprise value and support business objectives
• Strong commercial and financial acumen, including expertise in sourcing, negotiations, supplier economics, total cost of ownership (TCO), contracting, and value management
• Subject-matter expertise: in:Regulatory and Pharmacovigilance or similar: categories in healthcare, biotech: or pharmaceutical industry, particularly with the management of CRO supplier commercial partnerships:
• Track record of delivering measurable outcomes across cost optimization, productivity, innovation, business performance, risk management, and sustainability objectives
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage, challenge, and align senior leaders across functions, business units, and geographies
• Experience leveraging market intelligence, spend analytics, and data-driven insights to inform strategic decisions and identify value creation opportunities
• Strong supplier relationship management capabilities, including supplier segmentation, governance, performance management, and innovation partnership development

• Experience utilizing digital procurement technologies, advanced analytics, automation, and AI-enabled solutions to enhance decision-making and business outcomes
• Excellent leadership, communication, negotiation, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to influence outcomes and drive change in a dynamic environment

title: APAC Portfolio (Sr.) Manager
description:
Role Purpose
We are looking for an independent, commercially minded professional to join our Portfolio team and own the identification, evaluation, and advancement of novel pharmaceutical opportunities for our APAC markets, taking each opportunity from first signal to a clear recommendation and driving the agreed next steps.
The role will focus on innovative and differentiated assets, including NCEs, 505(b)(2) products, and other value-added pharmaceutical opportunities, assessing their strategic fit, value, and timing across our key APAC markets to decide where our time and resources are best invested.
The individual will work cross-functionally with Commercial, Medical, Regulatory, IP, Market Access, Business Development, Finance, and other internal teams, integrating their input into a single Portfolio view of each opportunity and a clear recommendation the business can act on.
Scope and Decision Rights
The Head of Portfolio APAC sets strategy, priorities, and major portfolio decisions. Within that framework, this role independently drives its own analyses, opportunities, and projects, makes recommendations, and executes the agreed actions. It is expected to move work forward without step-by-step approval and to judge when to involve others:
• Decides directly: how to scope and structure an evaluation, which data and internal experts to draw on, when a first answer is sufficient, and which opportunities to screen out against agreed criteria.
• Aligns with the Head of Portfolio APAC: recommendations to advance, pause, or stop an opportunity, changes to priorities, and positions to take with potential partners.
• Escalates: matters with material financial, legal, IP, or reputational impact, and cross-functional disagreements that cannot be resolved at working level.
Key Responsibilities
• Own an up-to-date view of the APAC opportunity pipeline across near-, mid-, and long-term horizons, flag gaps and imbalances, and recommend areas for expansion, investment, or rationalization.
• Proactively scan global markets, pipelines, and competitor activity to identify novel product opportunities relevant to APAC, and bring forward those worth pursuing with a clear rationale.
• Lead the evaluation of shortlisted opportunities end-to-end, integrating medical, clinical, IP, regulatory, development, commercial, competitive, and market-access perspectives with timing and economics, and scaling the depth of analysis to what the decision actually requires.
• Build a working understanding of treatment guidelines, clinical practice, patient pathways, unmet needs, and physician preferences in each market, and use it to judge whether an opportunity is genuinely differentiated against current and future standards of care.
• Assess competitive landscape, product differentiation, market potential, pricing, reimbursement, and positioning, distinguishing real, reachable opportunities from theoretical ones.
• Drive product evaluations to a conclusion with Commercial, Regulatory, IP, Market Access, Medical, and Business Development teams, involving the right people at the right time and reconciling conflicting inputs.
• Build patient-based forecasts, sales potential, and scenario analyses, making key assumptions explicit and identifying which of them drive the decision.
• Identify relevant companies and assets for partnering and licensing opportunities, and recommend, together with Business Development, which to prioritize and how to approach them.
• Plan and follow through on partnering conferences: prioritize target companies, products, and meetings beforehand, and turn outcomes into agreed next steps afterwards.
• Own follow-through on assigned opportunities, keeping evaluation status, partner interactions, and follow-up actions current, and making sure agreed actions are delivered.
• Present assigned areas in periodic portfolio reviews with management in decision-ready form, highlighting key risks, gaps, growth opportunities, the recommended course of action, and the decisions required.
Ways of Working
We are looking for someone who, given an objective and the context, works out how to get there: think, decide, act, and follow through. In practice, this means:
• Own the outcome, not just the task. Start from what needs to be achieved, structure the problem, find and analyze the information needed, reach a conclusion, and follow through until the agreed actions are delivered.
• Useful answers, fast. Produce a solid first answer quickly, be explicit about what is fact and what is assumption, identify what is missing, and go deeper only where it would change the decision.
• Always a recommendation. Analysis ends with a position, not a list of findings: “Based on this, I recommend X because Y, and the next step is Z.”
• Proactive. Spot risks and opportunities before being asked (in an asset, market, patent situation, launch opportunity, competitive development, or portfolio assumption), raise them early, and propose how to address them.
• Independent, not isolated. Move work forward without needing approval for each step, and know when to bring in Portfolio, BD, Commercial, Regulatory, IP, Medical, Finance, or other functions.
• Constructive challenge. Question assumptions, analyses, and proposed approaches when there is good reason to, explain why, and bring a better alternative.
• Clear and concise. Communicate across functions and geographies in a structured, commercially relevant way: what is happening, why it matters, what you think, and what we should do.
Preferred Profile
• Degree in Medicine, Pharmacy, Life Sciences, Biotechnology, or related field; MBA or equivalent business training is an advantage.
• Typically 5–8 years of experience in New Product Planning, Portfolio Strategy, Business Development, Commercial Strategy, Medical Affairs, or pharmaceutical consulting, including a track record of taking evaluations or projects through to a decision or outcome.
• Strong ability to interpret clinical data and translate it into commercial implications and portfolio recommendations.
• Strong analytical and forecasting skills, combined with the judgment to separate what matters from what does not and to know when an answer is good enough to act on.
• Intellectual curiosity about pharmaceutical innovation and emerging assets, with the commercial sense to tell an interesting asset from a real opportunity for the company.
• Working understanding of how IP, regulatory pathways (including 505(b)(2)), development, and market access shape the value and timing of an asset; deep expertise in every area is not required.
• Comfortable with ambiguity and incomplete information, and willing to take a position, defend it with evidence, and revise it when the evidence changes.
• Clear, concise communicator, effective with colleagues and partners across functions, cultures, and geographies.
While applying, please mention the APAC countries you have handled and one novel asset you have evaluated.

Preferred Experience

• Familiarity with e-sourcing, contract lifecycle management, spend analytics and supplier-management platforms.

title: Procurement Manager
description:
We are looking for a Procurement Manager to own technology sourcing for IMC India. You will run the full cycle for IT hardware, software, network, data centre and technology services: from understanding what our engineers and traders need, to negotiating with vendors, to managing contracts and renewals.
You will work closely with Technology, Infrastructure, Information Security, Legal, Compliance and Finance in Mumbai, and with IMC's global procurement colleagues in other offices. You will also lead and develop a small team.
Key spend categories: servers, storage and low-latency network hardware; software licences and SaaS; data centre and colocation; telecom and leased lines; cloud services; end-user devices; IT services and support contracts; market data and connectivity.
Your Core Responsibilities
Sourcing and negotiation
• Identify new vendors and service providers in India and globally, building a strong supplier base for each IT category.
• Run end-to-end sourcing for IT categories: requirements, RFI/RFQ/RFP, vendor evaluation, commercial negotiation and award.
• Negotiate pricing, SLAs, support terms, warranties, delivery timelines and licensing models with OEMs, distributors and service providers.
• Manage urgent hardware buys for trading infrastructure, balancing speed with cost and control.
• Reduce single-vendor dependency by identifying and maintaining alternative suppliers for strategic and critical categories
Market intelligence and forward planning
• Track IT market trends, pricing and supply conditions, such as rising memory, storage and GPU costs, component shortages, lead times and currency movements, and brief stakeholders on what they mean for IMC.
• Build close relationships with IT and infrastructure teams to understand upcoming needs early, and with vendors and OEMs to get early sight of price changes, product roadmaps and end-of-life notices.
• Use this insight to anticipate supply constraints and price rises and act ahead of them, for example by timing purchases, securing allocation or locking in pricing, and to spot savings opportunities.
Contracts and vendor management
• Review and negotiate MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, licence agreements and DPAs with Legal.
• Keep a contract register and renewal calendar so no licence, support contract or circuit lapses unplanned.
• Run vendor onboarding, due diligence and periodic performance reviews against SLAs and KPIs.
• Manage relationships with strategic technology vendors and escalate issues when needed.
Risk, compliance and controls
• Work with Information Security and Compliance on third-party risk assessments, especially for vendors with access to systems or data.
• Work with Finance to handle tax aspects of purchases, including GST, TDS, import duties and documentation for imported hardware.
• Keep procurement auditable: approvals, purchase orders, three-way match and documentation ready for internal and external audit.
• Partner with IT on hardware asset lifecycle: procurement, tagging, refresh cycles and compliant disposal (e-waste).
Budget, reporting and team
• Support annual IT budgeting and forecasting with Finance and Technology leads.
• Report on spend, savings, contract status and vendor performance.
• Improve procurement processes and tools, including the purchase-to-pay workflow.
• Lead, coach and develop 1–2 procurement specialists.
Your Skills And Experience
• 8–12 years in procurement, with at least 5 years focused on IT or technology categories.
• Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, supply chain or a related field. An MBA or a certification such as CIPS or CPSM is a plus.
• Solid understanding of IT hardware, networking, software licensing models (perpetual, subscription, enterprise agreements) and cloud pricing.
• Strong negotiation skills and a record of measurable savings and better contract terms.
• Experience drafting and negotiating technology contracts and SLAs.
• Working knowledge of Indian procurement requirements: GST, TDS, import and customs processes, and vendor compliance.
• Experience in financial services, trading, or another regulated, technology-heavy environment is strongly preferred.
• Comfort with ERP and procurement tools [e.g. Workday, Coupa, SAP Ariba] and strong Excel skills.
• Clear communicator who can work with engineers, traders, legal and finance, and with global colleagues across time zones.
• Experience managing or mentoring a small team.
• Experience buying data centre or colocation services, low-latency network equipment or market data.
• Exposure to third-party risk management frameworks and information security questionnaires.
• Experience with software asset management (SAM) tools.
About Us
IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

title: Healthcare Procurement Manager (Medical Equipment)
description:
Category Buyer – Medical Equipment
Department: Procurement & Supply Chain (Corporate Headquarters)
 Location: Head Office (Corporate)
 Experience: ~10–12 years (Mid-level)
 Reporting to: Head – Procurement / Supply Chain
 Employment Type: Full-Time 
Position Overview / Role Purpose
The Category Buyer – Medical Equipment is responsible for leading the strategic sourcing and end-to-end procurement of high-value medical equipment across the organization’s healthcare facilities. This mid-level role (approximately 10+ years’ experience) integrates clinical requirements, technical evaluation, and commercial strategy to ensure cost optimization, equipment standardization, regulatory compliance, and supply continuity across the healthcare network. The Category Buyer collaborates closely with cross-functional teams to align procurement plans with clinical needs and organizational growth, while driving digitization, sustainability, and process excellence. 
Key Responsibilities
1. Category Strategy & Planning:
• Develop and execute category strategy for medical equipment procurement, aligned with business goals and expansion plans. 
• Standardize equipment specifications and SKUs across hospitals to leverage scale and ensure consistency in product use. 
• Annual planning & forecasting: Prepare annual procurement plans, consolidate demand across facilities, and support CAPEX budgeting/forecasting for medical equipment. 
• Market intelligence: Track market trends, technological advancements, and supplier innovations to inform procurement decisions and support future projects. 
2. Procurement & Contract Management:
• End-to-end sourcing: Lead the full procurement lifecycle – from requirements gathering and tender/RFP processes to technical evaluations, negotiations, contracting, and supplier onboarding. 
• Commercial negotiations: Negotiate favorable pricing, terms, and service-level agreements for equipment purchases, including annual rate contracts (ARC) and long-term agreements with key vendors. 
• Contract administration: Manage Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC), Comprehensive Maintenance Contracts (CMC), warranties, and long-term service agreements, ensuring compliance with terms and maximizing equipment uptime. 
3. Financial & Cost Management:
• Cost optimization: Drive cost-saving initiatives and value-based procurement across the medical equipment category, closely monitoring pricing benchmarks and achieving targeted annual savings (e.g. 5–10% reduction in category spend). 
• Budget alignment: Ensure all procurement activities align with CAPEX/OPEX budgets and financial strategies, maintaining fiscal discipline while meeting clinical needs. 
• Total cost of ownership: Evaluate equipment purchases based on lifecycle costs and return on investment, balancing upfront price with long-term maintenance, operations, and disposal costs. 
4. Technical Evaluation & Compliance:
• Coordinate technical assessments of equipment with clinicians, biomedical engineers, and end-users to ensure equipment meets clinical requirements and specifications. 
• Techno-commercial evaluations: Conduct thorough technical and commercial evaluations of bids, comparing functionality, quality, and total cost to select best-value solutions. 
• Regulatory compliance: Ensure all equipment and procurement processes comply with healthcare regulations and quality standards (e.g., NABH, JCI, and local medical device regulations) and internal procurement governance policies. 
• Lifecycle management: Oversee the entire lifecycle of critical equipment – from acquisition through installation, maintenance (with service contracts), and end-of-life disposal – maximizing asset utilization and ensuring continuous availability of essential equipment. 
5. Vendor & Stakeholder Management:
• Supplier partnerships: Develop a strong vendor ecosystem, nurturing strategic partnerships with Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and distributors to secure reliable supply and innovation support. 
• Vendor performance: Implement supplier scorecards and track key vendor performance metrics (e.g., on-time-in-full delivery (OTIF), quality, service level compliance) to drive continuous improvement and accountability. 
• Collaboration: Work closely with key stakeholders – including clinical departments, hospital administrators, finance, biomedical engineering, operations, and project teams – to align procurement decisions with operational needs and ensure seamless equipment deployment. 
• Issue resolution: Address supplier issues, manage supply risks, and maintain supply continuity for critical equipment across the network.
6. Governance, Risk & Process Excellence:
• Policy & SOP adherence: Implement and uphold robust procurement policies, SOPs and ethical standards, ensuring transparent processes and audit-ready documentation. 
• Digital procurement & analytics: Drive digitization of procurement through e-procurement platforms, spend analytics dashboards, and other digital tools, improving process efficiency, spend visibility, and data-driven decision making. 
• Audit and risk management: Ensure audit readiness, regulatory compliance, and effective risk mitigation strategies in procurement activities to maintain the highest standards of governance and supply chain resilience. 
• Sustainable & ESG-focused procurement: Integrate sustainability and ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) criteria into procurement decisions, prioritizing ethical sourcing and environmentally responsible suppliers to support long-term organizational values and compliance. 
Key Result Areas (KRAs) & Measurable Outcomes
Key Result Area (KRA)
Measurable Outcome/Target
Cost Optimization
Achieve 5–10% annual cost savings in medical equipment spend through strategic sourcing, standardization, and negotiations 
Procurement Efficiency
Reduce procurement lead times and cycle times, ensuring timely delivery and commissioning of equipment to meet project schedules 
Vendor Performance & Reliability
Improve supplier performance metrics (e.g., on-time delivery > 95% OTIF, reduced stock-outs) and consolidate vendor base to enhance supply reliability 
Compliance & Governance
100% audit compliance with procurement SOPs and regulatory standards; maintain audit-ready documentation with zero major non-compliances 
Digital & Process Excellence
Implement e-procurement systems and analytics dashboards covering full category spend for improved decision support and transparency 
Stakeholder & Project Support
High stakeholder satisfaction and timely project support, enabling on-schedule commissioning of new healthcare facilities and expansions 
Key Stakeholders / Interfaces
• Internal: Hospital CEOs/Administrators; Clinical & Nursing Leadership; Biomedical Engineering teams; Finance & Accounts; Project & Infrastructure teams; Hospital Operations & Supply Chain; Inventory/Stores; Quality & Accreditation (e.g. NABH/NABL) teams. 
• External: Suppliers/OEMs, distributors, and service providers for medical equipment and maintenance. 
Qualifications & Experience
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering, mechanical/electrical engineering, life sciences, or supply chain management; MBA or postgraduate qualification in Supply Chain, Operations or Healthcare Management preferred. 
• Experience: 10–12+ years of progressive experience in procurement/supply chain (with significant exposure to healthcare or medical equipment sourcing). Experience in hospital or healthcare group procurement is strongly preferred for understanding clinical and regulatory nuances. 
Core Competencies
• Strategic Sourcing & Category Management: Proven ability to develop and implement effective category strategies, with strong negotiation and contract management skills. 
• Techno-Commercial Acumen: Deep understanding of medical equipment technical specifications, and the ability to perform techno-commercial evaluations and lifecycle costing. 
• Healthcare Regulatory & Quality Knowledge: Familiarity with healthcare procurement standards and regulatory requirements, ensuring that equipment meets accreditation and compliance standards (e.g., NABH/JCI, medical device regulations). 
• Analytical & Financial Skills: Strong analytical mindset with competence in data-driven decision making, cost analysis, and budget management. 
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with clinical leaders, technical experts, and finance stakeholders, driving alignment and consensus across departments. 
• Results Orientation & Continuous Improvement: Focus on delivering measurable results (cost savings, efficiency, quality) and driving continuous improvements in procurement processes through best practices and innovation.
Tools & Systems
Proficiency with enterprise ERP and e-Procurement systems (e.g., SAP Ariba, Oracle, or similar) and analytics platforms (spend analytics, procurement dashboards) to support reporting and data-driven decision-making. Familiarity with digital procurement technologies, supplier management software, and advanced Excel/BI tools is expected as part of driving procurement digitization efforts.

title: Senior Financial Planner & Analyst
description:
FP&A / Business Finance
Role Overview
We are looking for a finance professional who can own planning, forecasting, management reporting, business analysis, working capital, and financial modelling in a high-growth environment.
We hire on demonstrated capability, not on credentials. The role requires strong financial ownership, analytical thinking, attention to detail, and the ability to translate financial data into actionable business insights.
Key Responsibilities
•  Planning & Forecasting
• Own the annual operating plan, a rolling 12-month forecast, and driver-based models and business plans built on volumes, pricing, bill-of-material cost and headcount, not last year plus a percentage.
•  Management Reporting & MIS
• Own the monthly pack for both entities and the consolidation, covering P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, KPIs and cost centres.
• Prepare sales and cost performance reporting, delivered to a fixed working day.
•  Dashboards & Business Reporting
• Build and maintain CEO, CFO, functional-head and investor dashboards.
• Ensure one definition per metric, with controls that prove the numbers tie.
•  Cash, Working Capital & Treasury
• Own the cash position statement and short-term cash forecast.
• Track receivables and payables ageing and collections, inventory ageing, DSO / DIO / DPO.
• Manage treasury and investment valuation summaries, along with the overall liquidity and runway view.
•  Variance Analysis
• Perform budget vs actual, forecast vs actual, month-on-month and year-on-year analysis.
• Decompose variances into volume, rate and mix.
• Provide the cause, impact and recommended action — not just the number.
•  Unit Economics & Pricing
• Analyse profitability by product, segment, customer and geography.
• Build cost structures from bill of material to commissioning.
• Provide deal-level margin support.
• Develop capital-expenditure and make-versus-buy business cases.
•  Board, Investor & Fundraising Support
• Support the financial sections of the board pack and investor MIS.
• Build the models, scenarios and diligence data required for a fundraise.
•  Market & Competitive Insight
• Conduct market sizing and demand analysis.
• Track competitors and perform benchmarking that informs business planning and pricing decisions.
•  Working Capital Improvement
• Drive working capital as an agenda, not just a report.
• Own a tracked improvement programme with named owners across sales, supply chain and procurement.
•  Automation & Process Improvement
• Move the reporting cycle from assembly to analysis.
• Use Power Query, a single mapped data layer, and clear documentation so that the reporting process can be independently run by anyone on the team the following month.
What We’re Looking For
We hire on demonstrated capability, not on credentials. A CA, CMA, MBA (Finance) or CFA would be relevant.
Core Experience & Capabilities
• 5 years in FP&A, business finance, management reporting or corporate finance, including an audit or advisory background with a deliberate move into analysis.
• Personally owned a monthly reporting pack for at least twelve consecutive cycles.
• Built a budget or forecast from drivers, not from last year plus a percentage.
• Written variance commentary that senior management acted on.
• Worked directly from a trial balance or an ERP extract, not only from clean data handed over to you.
• Strong advanced Excel and financial modelling skills.
• Power Query, Power BI or SQL is a strong plus.
• Have the instinct to say “this does not tie” before a pack goes out — and hold that line.
Good to Have
• Recurring ownership of receivables, payables and cash reporting.
• Experience in treasury or investment reporting.
• Multi-entity consolidation and multi-currency experience.
• Experience in manufacturing, hardware or supply-chain-intensive industries.
• Experience with market sizing or competitive benchmarking for a management audience.

title: Finance Analyst – Pricing & Financial Modeling
description:
Job Description 
This role is primarily focused on FP&A, pricing analysis, financial modeling, and scenario/what-if analysis. The Finance Analyst will build and maintain robust, decision-ready financial models, run scenario-based analyses to support pricing and business decisions, and provide the analytical backbone for FP&A reporting. Advanced Excel modeling skills are essential to this role. The candidate will partner closely with Finance, Solutions, Operations, and leadership to translate business questions into structured financial models and scenarios.
Key Responsibilities 
Pricing, Modeling & Scenario Analysis (Core Focus) 
● Own end-to-end financial model development and maintenance, including integrated revenue, expense, and
headcount models.
● Build and maintain pricing models, including deal-level and customer-level pricing analysis.
● Design and run scenario-based / what-if models to evaluate the financial impact of pricing changes, cost
structures, and business decisions.
● Perform sensitivity analysis on key business drivers (volume, price, cost, mix) to support leadership
decision-making.
● Support ad hoc initiatives including pricing strategy, deal evaluation, and acquisition-related financial
modeling and scenario analysis.
● Develop and automate dashboards, KPI reporting, and streamlined data flows to support modeling and
scenario work across systems.
FP&A, Reporting & Planning Support 
● Prepare project-level cost reporting and insights.
● Prepare COGS and operating expense (Opex) variance analysis reports.
● Prepare customer- and vertical-level margin reporting.
● Deliver performance insights and executive-level reporting, including variance analysis.
● Manage monthly and quarterly forecasting cycles with cross-functional alignment.
● Drive the annual budgeting process in coordination with internal and outsourced accounting teams.
● Partner across teams to improve data quality, governance, and system integration.
Requirements 
● Very strong, hands-on Excel skills are essential — advanced financial modeling, scenario-based modeling,
and what-if analysis (sensitivity tables, data tables, scenario manager, dynamic driver-based models).
● Demonstrated experience building pricing models and conducting pricing analysis.
● Demonstrated expertise in financial modelling, planning systems, and performance reporting.
● Strong understanding of budgeting cycles, forecasting processes, and financial governance.
● Strong analytical thinking, accuracy, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate business needs
into scalable financial models and automation.
● Excellent communication skills, with the ability to partner with senior leadership and cross-functional
stakeholders.
● Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment, and collaborate
effectively with outsourced/shared service teams.
● Experience in healthcare services, and/or PE-backed environments is an advantage.
Qualifications 
● Masters degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.
● Professional certifications (e.g., CFA, CMA) or an MBA (Finance) are preferred but not required.
● Subject Matter Expert in Excel — advanced financial modeling, scenario/what-if analysis, and pricing
models; Google Sheets modeling experience is also acceptable. BI experience (Power BI, Tableau, Looker)
is preferred.
● 5 to 10 years of experience in FP&A, pricing, strategic finance, or financial modeling roles.

title: Acquisition Analyst
description:
Role Purpose
The Acquisition Analyst will evaluate new investments, support opportunistic M&A/divestitures, and enable disciplined capital allocation. The role blends valuation, financial modelling, market analysis, and cross‑functional coordination to drive decision‑quality insights for senior leadership and boards.
Key Responsibilities
1) Strategic Investment Analysis & Capital Allocation
• Build detailed return, scenario, and sensitivity analyses for new growth and acquisition opportunities; recommend capital deployment aligned to long‑term priorities and investor objectives.
• Apply a structured investment framework and governance thresholds to ensure disciplined allocation of capital.
2) Portfolio Valuation & Modelling (REIT & Office)
• Support valuation of the REIT; develop/maintain cash‑flow models reflecting operating drivers and market dynamics.
• Contribute to periodic business plan updates and asset strategy reviews; track performance against plan and recommend corrective actions.
3) Mergers, Acquisitions & Divestitures (Opportunistic)
• Assist in due diligence, valuation, synergy thinking, and coordination of internal workstreams and external advisors for M&A/divestiture processes.
• Drive timelines, data rooms, and issue logs to seamlessly execute transactions.
4) Financial Planning & Performance Analysis
• Support budgeting, forecasting, and five‑year planning, ensuring linkage to strategic initiatives and REIT/portfolio objectives.
• Prepare monthly/quarterly variance and driver analyses, dashboards, and insight memos for leadership.
6) Board, Investor & Executive‑Level Reporting
• Prepare Board decks, Investment Committee notes, and monthly business reviews; translate complex financial/operational data into clear, executive‑ready insights.
• Support investor presentations and REIT reporting cycles.
8) Opportunity Screening & Contractual Analysis
• Act as the first filter for new investment opportunities arising under customer contracts and the Shareholders Agreement (SHA); test fit against predefined criteria.
• Coordinate cross‑functional inputs and approvals to drive timely decisions.
9) JV Asset Funding & Reimbursement
• Build models for capital vs. debt allocations for each JV asset; recommend optimal funding mix.
• Manage reimbursement calculations for founding shareholder investments in speculative builds transferred to the JV.
10) Market Research & Competitive Intelligence
• Conduct ongoing market research and competitive landscape analysis to inform valuations, underwriting assumptions, and portfolio strategy.
Qualifications
Education
• MBA (Tier‑1) or CA (Rank Holder) preferred; prior commercial real estate experience strongly preferred.
Experience
• 1-3 years in investment analysis, corporate finance/FP&A, transaction support (M&A), real estate private equity, or REITs.

title: Analyst/ Senior Analyst – Corporate Finance
description:
About DESRI
DESRI (formerly D. E. Shaw Renewable Investments) is a market-leading owner and operator of renewable energy projects throughout the United States. We have acquired or developed approximately 11.9 gigawatts of contracted capacity across a portfolio of over 80 renewable energy projects in 24 states. DESRI is run by a dynamic team with offices located at New York, Denver, and Hyderabad (India).
About The Role
We are looking for a resourceful and driven professional to join DESRI, based out of the firm’s Hyderabad, India office. The successful candidate will be a part of a small, inclusive, highly skilled team responsible for supporting DESRI’s portfolio of wind, solar and battery projects in an agile environment that values collaboration, thoughtful problem solving, and attention to detail.
What You'll Do
You will work on a wide variety of Treasury and Corporate Finance initiatives, with a substantial focus on Corporate Finance, managing our corporate-level debt facilities, and Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A). On the Corporate Finance/FP&A side, you will be responsible for forecasting DESRI’s short-term and long-term cash position, both at the project and corporate levels, tracking overall deal flow, planning for upcoming significant fundings, identifying and alleviating liquidity and covenant compliance concerns, and optimizing distributions. You will also need to use various existing forecasting and budgeting tools in this process, while striving to build them out further and implement new ones to streamline, consolidate, and broaden DESRI’s forecasting capabilities. You will also work on other areas of corporate finance, such as working with lenders, investors, counsel, and senior management on the initiation, modeling, due diligence, closing, and ongoing
compliance of corporate financing facilities.
Additionally, you will work with various stakeholders, including bankers, investors, senior management, asset managers, and the accounting team, to ensure that the cash side of the business is functioning efficiently while continuously developing and implementing process improvements. Furthermore, you will be responsible for preparing periodic reports for the financing parties and senior management. Additionally, this position offers an opportunity to work on initiatives related to establishing, standardizing, optimizing, and documenting corporate finance processes, workflows, and controls.
Qualifications
The ideal candidate should hold –
• Education: Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Finance or a Chartered Accountant (CA) degree
• Experience: 1-2 years of experience in Treasury, Corporate Finance, FP&A, or Accounting-related functions.
• Skills: Strong financial modeling and analytical skills; proficiency with forecasting and budgeting tools; effective written and verbal communication skills; ability to develop strong partnerships and influence stakeholders across teams.

description:

As Business Finance Manager, you will own budgeting, forecasting, and financial performance across CureMeAbroad. You will partner with sales, operations, and the founding team to plan expenditure, protect margins across our 350+ partner network, and maintain predictable cash flow.

Conduct monthly budget-versus-actual reviews and drive corrective actions based on variances.

Build financial models for new markets, partnerships, and pricing strategies.
Analyse unit economics across individual patient cases, countries, and partner hospitals.
3. Business Partnering
Partner with sales, operations, and marketing teams on financial planning and decision-making.
Evaluate business cases, track Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and channel ROI, and support negotiations with hospitals and vendors.
4. Cash Flow & Treasury Management
Manage cash flow, working capital, and financial liquidity.
Monitor foreign exchange (FX) exposure and oversee the reconciliation of patient payments, refunds, and partner payouts.
5. Reporting, Controls & Compliance
Ensure accurate monthly financial closes and management information system (MIS) reporting.
Strengthen financial controls, approval workflows, and internal processes.
Support GST, TDS, FEMA/RBI compliance, audits, and investor reporting.

Mentor and guide finance executives.
Improve financial reporting tools, automation, and processes to enhance efficiency and accuracy.

2–6 years of experience in FP&A, business finance, or financial controllership.
# Education: 
CA, CMA, MBA (Finance), or an equivalent qualification.
# Financial Expertise: 
Strong knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and translating financial analysis into actionable business decisions.

Hands-on experience with multi-currency transactions, cross-border payment flows, foreign exchange, and relevant regulatory requirements.

Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills, experience with Tally, Zoho Books, QuickBooks, SAP, or similar accounting systems, and familiarity with BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau.

Global Impact: Be part of a global medical tourism technology and discovery platform connecting patients from high-cost markets such as the US, UK, Germany, and Australia with verified hospitals and surgeons across India, Turkey, Thailand, Mexico, and Spain.
Fast-Paced Growth: Join a fast-scaling global medical tourism brand.
High Ownership: Take ownership of financial planning and performance, with a direct influence on business decisions and growth.
Leadership Exposure: Work directly with the founding team on live deals, international markets, and real business growth targets.

title: Financial Planning and Analysis Manager
company: Pramod Confectionary And Food Industries Limited
description:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Head of Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for leading enterprise-wide financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance analysis. This role partners with the CFO and executive leadership to provide data-driven insights that inform strategic decision-making, optimize capital allocation, and drive business transformation. The successful candidate will establish best practices in financial modeling, governance, and analytics while building and mentoring a high-performing FP&A team.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Financial Planning & Budgeting
• Lead annual budget cycle including revenue forecasting, expense planning, and headcount modeling across all business units and departments
• Develop rolling forecasts (quarterly and annual) updated monthly to reflect actuals and business dynamics; integrate with strategic plans
• Design and implement budget governance framework, approval workflows, and accountability mechanisms; ensure alignment with corporate strategy
Financial Analysis & Reporting
• Conduct comprehensive variance analysis; explain monthly/quarterly performance vs. budget and prior year; identify trends and risk indicators
• Build P&L analysis by business unit, product line, geography, customer segment, and channel to identify profitability drivers and optimization opportunities
• Prepare executive dashboards and board-level financial reports; ensure metrics are material, actionable, and tracked against KPIs
Strategic & Ad Hoc Analysis
• Support mergers & acquisitions, divestitures, and partnership evaluations with valuation models, sensitivity analysis, and integration planning
• Lead pricing strategy analysis, margin optimization, and profitability modeling for new products, markets, or business models
• Conduct capital allocation studies; recommend investment priorities across R&D, marketing, operations, and IT initiatives
Systems, Tools & Governance
• Own FP&A technology roadmap; evaluate, implement, and optimize planning systems (e.g., Anaplan, Vena, Workday Planning) and BI tools
• Establish FP&A playbook including standards for model building, documentation, review, and change control; audit models annually for accuracy and governance
• Ensure data governance, integrity, and security; coordinate with Accounting, IT, and Business teams to align data definitions and reconciliation protocols
Team Leadership & Development
• Recruit, mentor, and develop FP&A team; create career paths and training programs; drive a culture of analytical rigor and continuous improvement
• Establish FP&A competency model; conduct performance reviews; identify and address skill gaps and high-potential talent
• Foster collaboration across Finance, Accounting, Operations, and Business units; communicate findings in clear, executive-friendly language
KEY RESULT AREAS (KRAs)
1. Annual Budget & Rolling Forecast Leadership
• Establish budget calendar; manage timeline, stakeholder engagement, and consolidation process
• Deliver balanced, achievable budget; stress-test against market scenarios and corporate initiatives
• Maintain monthly rolling forecast; update revenue drivers, cost assumptions, and headcount based on business performance and strategy
2. Variance Analysis & Performance Insights
• Analyze monthly/quarterly variance; articulate root causes (volume, price, mix, cost, timing)
• Identify emerging trends, risk indicators, and upside opportunities; escalate material issues to CFO/CEO
• Support business unit leaders in deep dives; facilitate variance review meetings with executive team
3. Financial Modeling & Scenario Analysis
• Build dynamic, flexible models for P&L, cash flow, DCF, and sensitivity analysis
• Develop scenario models for strategic options (e.g., market expansion, M&A, restructuring); test impact on profitability and cash flow
• Ensure models are auditable, well-documented, and maintained for ongoing use and refinement
4. Executive Reporting & Dashboarding
• Design and maintain KPI dashboards for management and board review; refresh monthly/quarterly
• Prepare board packs and management presentations with clear, data-driven narratives
• Communicate results to non-financial executives in business impact language
5. Strategic & M&A Analytics
• Lead financial due diligence on acquisition targets; build valuation and integration financial models
• Support pricing, product profitability, and product portfolio optimization initiatives
• Conduct ROI tracking on capital projects and strategic initiatives; measure actual results vs. projection
6. Systems, Process & Automation Excellence
• Implement and optimize FP&A technology stack (EPM, BI, data integration tools)
• Automate manual processes; standardize reporting and model templates; reduce cycle time
• Establish data governance, security, and quality standards; reconcile FP&A data to GL
7. Team Development & Capability Building
• Hire and train FP&A analysts and managers; build bench strength in financial modeling, data analysis, and executive communication
• Mentor high-potential talent; sponsor career development and external training
• Foster knowledge sharing and best practices across the FP&A function; conduct monthly team huddles and quarterly strategy reviews
8. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence
• Partner with business unit leaders on planning and performance management; ensure alignment of goals and KPIs
• Coordinate with Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and Investor Relations; align reporting and disclosures
• Collaborate with IT and Data teams on system implementations and data pipelines
REQUIRED COMPETENCIES & SKILLS
Competency
Description
Evidence / Experience
Financial Acumen
Deep understanding of financial statements, accounting, and corporate finance; ability to build models and analyze scenarios
CPA or CFA preferred; advanced Excel (VBA, Power Query); SQL and/or Python for data manipulation
Business Acumen
Understanding of business model, value drivers, competitive dynamics, and growth/profitability levers
7+ years FP&A/corporate finance in high-growth or public company; background in relevant industry preferred
Strategic Thinking
Ability to connect financial insights to strategy; recommend actions aligned with corporate objectives
Track record of contributing to strategic decisions; experience with M&A or major business transformations
Leadership
Ability to lead, develop, and motivate analytical teams; influence peers across functions without direct authority
Managed FP&A or finance teams of 4+; strong feedback; tenure and promotion track record
Communication
Ability to simplify complex financial analysis; present to C-suite; communicate with non-financial audience
Presentations to board/executives; ability to write clear memos; strong listening and collaboration skills
Technical Skills
Proficiency in business intelligence tools, planning software, and data integration platforms
Tableau/Power BI, Anaplan/Vena, Workday Planning, SAP, NetSuite, or Salesforce analytics experience
EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION
• 7+ years of FP&A, corporate finance, or management consulting experience
• 3+ years in a leadership role managing FP&A or finance teams
• Experience in a high-growth or public company environment preferred
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field (MBA or CPA/CFA preferred)
• Demonstrable experience building financial models and using planning/BI software
FIRST-YEAR SUCCESS METRICS
Months 1-3: Immersion & Assessment
• Establish FP&A roadmap and gaps analysis; document current processes and systems
• Meet with key stakeholders (business units, CFO, board); understand strategic priorities and pain points
Months 3-6: Quick Wins & Foundation
• Deliver improved budget accuracy and faster close cycle time
• Establish FP&A playbook and model governance standards
• Complete first quarterly business review with refreshed variance analysis and insights

title: Financing & Risk Solutions Associate
description:
Join us as a Financing & Risk Solutions Associate
• In this crucial role, you’ll work with business management in assessing business performance using various measures including customer satisfaction, revenue and capital efficiency
• We’ll look to you to support senior originators in building and maintaining the business with target client base
• This is a fantastic opportunity to hone your skills since you will be developing domain expertise in the businesses, supported through trainings, self-development and internal rotation
• We're offering this role at associate level
What you'll do
As a Financing & Risk Solutions Associate, you will be supporting the effective management of transactions to make sure that all activities are in line with the bank’s policies covering conduct, operational, credit, and regulatory risks.
Additionally, you’ll be preparing analysis, pitching materials, term sheets, post-transaction reviews and other documentation to support origination activities. You’ll also be assisting with client deep dives, navigating the sales coverage teams and gathering feedback from internal client touchpoints.
Your Day-to-day Activities Will Be
• Preparing pitch-books including investor presentations, analysing market dynamics, identifying market trends, generating trade ideas and other marketing materials
• Preparing corporate finance advisory materials and models covering the US technology space
• Tracking US and European markets and preparing market update slides on investment grade, high yield and leveraging loan markets
• Writing weekly market commentary for circulation to clients, updating and maintaining internal databases such as transaction issuance, investor order books, pricing analysis, deal reviews

You’ll have working knowledge of financial databases like Bloomberg, Intex, Reuters, Factset and Dealogic, along with an excellent understanding of financial statements including profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow.
Additionally, it will be an advantage if you have already worked in US markets and hold corporate finance or equity research experience, along with knowledge of various debt products and markets.
You’ll Also Demonstrate
• Experience of working in a daily cash management, fixed income, investment banking or credit research analytics function supporting a debt business
• Knowledge of investment banking and credit related products
• Strong knowledge of ratio analysis, key drivers for various sectors, pitch books and basic financial modelling
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationship with key stakeholders
• Excellent analytical and numerical skills as well as strong problem solving and logical thinking skills

title: Global Capital Market - Associate, Infra Capital Markets (Mumbai)
description:
Company Profile
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 42 countries.
As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career - a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.
Department Profile
Morgan Stanley is a worldwide leader in investment banking and is one of the top firms in mergers and acquisitions, underwriting of equity and equity-related transactions, corporate debt issuance, and high-yield debt financing. With professionals in 30 countries, we are consistently recognized for our performance in both traditional and innovative financing techniques, helping a wide range of clients around the world to make and execute decisions about their business strategy and financial structure.
We are looking for a Global Capital Markets professional focussed on Infrastructure Capital Markets business to join our Global Center in Mumbai. The analyst will support the origination, structuring, execution, syndication, and portfolio management of financing transactions across the infrastructure sector, with a focus on renewable energy, energy transition, tax equity, tax credit transferability, and high-yield / leveraged debt financings.
The Analyst will work closely with senior team members, counsel, risk, credit, finance, treasury, and senior management to execute complex structured financings for solar, storage, wind, power, and broader infrastructure assets. The role offers exposure to financial modelling, transaction structuring, and ongoing portfolio management.
You will receive variety of trainings covering financial analysis, business presentations, and practical skills. At the end of training, you will be able to understand financial concepts and have a strong understanding of the Morgan Stanley culture. In this role, you will gain exposure to financial markets and macro trends, build knowledge of banking and capital markets sectors and products, and work with bankers in core locations. High performers will be eligible for internal mobility opportunities globally.
Key Responsibilities
• Supporting transaction execution across tax equity, tax credit transfer, high-yield, project finance, and structured debt financings
• Building, reviewing, and maintaining financial models, including project finance models, tax equity models, credit models, valuation analyses, and portfolio projection models
• Preparing client materials, pitch books, investment memoranda, credit approval materials, syndication materials, and internal committee presentations
• Assisting with due diligence, including review of project documents, financing agreements, third-party reports, operating data, financial statements, tax assumptions, and sponsor materials
• Supporting underwriting and credit analysis, including assessment of cash flows, downside cases, leverage capacity, repayment risk, sponsor strength, collateral value, and structural protections
• Coordinating transaction workstreams across internal teams
• Assisting in the pre-work for negotiation and execution of financing documentation, tax equity agreements, tax credit transfer documentation, debt documents, and syndication materials
• Supporting ongoing portfolio management, including tracking asset performance, reviewing operating and financial reporting, reconciling distributions, updating projection models, monitoring covenant compliance, and preparing internal portfolio updates
• Contribute to process improvement, automation, and technical initiatives aimed at improving data accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of DCM workflows
• Provide ad-hoc analytical and operational support to meet evolving business needs and ensure smooth execution across transactions
The ideal candidate will have 1–2 years of experience in investment banking, leveraged finance, project finance, infrastructure, energy, credit, structured finance, or related capital markets roles.
Experience with renewable energy, power, tax equity, tax credit transferability, project finance, high-yield debt, leveraged finance, or structured credit is strongly preferred but not required.
Skills And Qualifications
• MBA / CA / Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent Keen interest in Capital Markets and intellectual curiosity Strong financial modelling ability and sound credit judgement
• Written competency and spoken language fluency in English
• Good communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate effectively with global teams
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills and comfort in working with large datasets
• Agility and ability to multi-task and thrive in a fast-paced environment
• Team player with a strong work ethic and motivation to learn
• Exceptional attention to detail, strong Excel and PowerPoint skills; familiarity with Bloomberg and market data tools (Bondradar, Dealogic, Pitchbook)
• Ability to manage expectations and handle high-pressure situations
• Programming and coding experience / knowledge of AI tools is encouraged
What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley
At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.
To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.
Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.
Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences.

title: Senior Associate - Merger and Acquisition
description:
Designation: Associate – Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A), Investments & Investor Relations
Experience: 3–4 years
Function: Corporate Finance / Strategy / Investments
Role Overview 
We are looking for a hands-on, analytically strong professional to support the organisation’s Mergers & Acquisitions, investment analysis, financial modelling, due diligence and Investor Relations (IR) activities. The role will involve working closely with senior leadership on investment opportunities, strategic transactions, financial analysis and investor-related deliverables. 
The ideal candidate should possess a strong foundation in financial analysis, investment research, financial modelling and preparation of Investment Committee (IC) notes, along with the ability to coordinate due diligence processes and manage multiple workstreams independently. The candidate should also be comfortable leveraging traditional financial tools as well as emerging AI-powered tools to enhance research, analysis and execution efficiency. 
Key Responsibilities 
1. M&A and Investment Analysis 
 •   Support the evaluation of potential M&A opportunities, strategic investments, acquisitions and other corporate finance initiatives.   
 •   Conduct industry, sector and company-level research to identify investment opportunities and assess business fundamentals.   
 •   Analyse financial statements, business performance, growth drivers, risks and investment viability.   
 •   Assist in valuation exercises using methodologies such as DCF, comparable company analysis and precedent transactions.   
 •   Prepare investment teasers, opportunity assessments and preliminary investment evaluation reports.   
2. Financial Modelling and Investment Committee (IC) Notes 
 •   Develop, maintain and update financial models, valuation models, business forecasts and scenario analyses.   
 •   Prepare detailed Investment Committee notes, investment memos, presentations and decision-support documents.   
 •   Translate complex financial and business information into clear, concise and actionable insights for senior management.   
 •   Conduct sensitivity analysis, assess key investment assumptions and evaluate potential returns and risks.   
 •   Support the preparation of financial projections, transaction analysis and investment recommendations.   
3. Due Diligence and Transaction Coordination 
 •   Coordinate financial, commercial, legal and operational due diligence with internal teams and external advisors.   
 •   Manage data rooms, maintain due diligence trackers and follow up on information requirements and transaction milestones.   
 •   Consolidate findings from multiple stakeholders, identify key risks and highlight material observations.   
 •   Assist in preparing transaction documentation, management presentations and other deal-related materials.   
 •   Track action items, timelines and deliverables to ensure the smooth execution of transaction workstreams.   
4. Investor Relations (IR) and Management Support 
 •   Support the preparation of investor presentations, performance updates, financial summaries and other investor-facing materials.   
 •   Assist in developing management reports, business updates and strategic presentations for investors and other stakeholders.   
 •   Conduct market, peer and competitor benchmarking to support investor communication and strategic decision-making.   
 •   Ensure accuracy, consistency and timely collation of financial and business information used in investor-related deliverables.   
 •   Provide analytical and execution support to senior leadership on ad hoc strategic, financial and business initiatives.   
5. Research, Analytics and AI-Enabled Productivity 
 •   Leverage traditional research platforms, financial databases and analytical tools to support investment evaluation and decision-making.   
 •   Use AI-powered tools to accelerate research, information synthesis, financial analysis, document review and presentation development.   
 •   Explore and implement efficient workflows using AI tools while ensuring data confidentiality, source validation and analytical accuracy.   
 •   Stay updated on industry developments, transaction trends, valuation benchmarks and emerging investment themes.   
Desired Candidate Profile 
 •   3–4 years of relevant experience in M&A, investment banking, corporate finance, transaction advisory, private equity, investment analysis or a similar role.   
 •   Strong hands-on experience in financial modelling, valuation, investment analysis and preparation of IC notes or investment memos.   
 •   Exposure to due diligence coordination and transaction execution is highly desirable.   
 •   Working knowledge of Investor Relations, investor presentations or management reporting would be an advantage.   
 •   Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to build financial models and develop high-quality presentations.   
 •   Familiarity with financial research platforms and AI tools for research, analysis and productivity.   
 •   Strong analytical, quantitative and problem-solving skills, with exceptional attention to detail.   
 •   Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex information clearly.   
 •   A proactive, execution-oriented approach, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced environment.   
Educational Qualifications 
 •   CA, MBA (Finance), CFA, or a postgraduate qualification in Finance, Economics or a related discipline.   
 •   Candidates with a strong finance and analytical foundation, relevant transaction exposure and demonstrable modelling skills will be preferred.   
Key Competencies 
 •   Financial and investment acumen   
 •   Financial modelling and valuation   
 •   Research and analytical rigour   
 •   Transaction and stakeholder coordination   
 •   Business writing and presentation skills   
 •   AI-enabled research and productivity   
 •   Ownership, agility and attention to detail
