description:
Job Description
Job Posting Description:
Security & Resiliency Initiative (SRI) is a cross-functional, capital-led program to identify risks in strategic supply chains and deploy financing and advisory solutions—often in partnership with the public sector—to enhance economic security and operational resilience in critical industries.
Join the team that is supporting J.P. Morgan's SRI business across the globe. The role involves supporting the banking team as part of the Centralized Research Group (CRG) by preparing pitch books and marketing materials, working on deep research, financial valuations, and other supporting materials.
Job Summary
As SRI Associate within CRG, you will be responsible for delivering high-impact, resilience-focused solutions across critical sectors. You will integrate deep research, financial analysis, and advanced Artificial intelligence (AI) / Large Language Model (LLM) methods to craft investment theses and assess opportunities. You will develop polished, insight-rich presentations and materials for senior clients and internal committees. You will help shape a cutting-edge practice that advances the decade-long commitment to national economic security.
Job Responsibilities
• Work closely with the SRI teams across the globe and support in preparing pitch books & marketing materials that the senior client bankers take to their clients during meetings
• Analyze markets, policies, and supply chains to identify structural risks and resilience opportunities across priority sectors
• Develop and refine investment theses, business cases, and impact assessments to guide capital allocation
• Conduct valuation and transaction analyses including Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), trading comps, transaction comps, and Leveraged Buyouts (LBOs)
• Prepare and deliver high-quality materials, internal memos, and committee presentations with executive-ready narratives
• Structure innovative, public-private and blended-finance solutions that align capital, policy, and execution
• Apply AI/LLM tools to accelerate research, generate insights, and enhance quality and speed of deliverables
• Coordinate diligence and risk assessments for complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives
• Drive continuous improvement of playbooks, templates, and research methods
Required Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills
• Excellent academic record
• 3+ years of experience in Investment Banking, Research, Consulting, SRI, Big Four experience or related field
• CA or MBA qualification
• Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with the ability to synthesize large amounts of information and help develop innovative client solutions
• Advanced user of MS Office suite, including Word and PowerPoint
• Close attention to detail and ability to work at very high standards of precision under tight deadlines
• Ability to work in a team environment
• Outstanding written and verbal communication skills
• Ensure the highest ethical standards and regulatory compliance within the firm
Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills
• Experience in sectors critical to economic security (e.g., supply chain, defense, energy, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, critical infrastructure, technology, healthcare)
• Familiarity with supply chain dynamics, industrial policy, national security-related economics, or government programs relevant to public-private investment
• Exposure to blended finance, risk-sharing structures, and public-private partnerships
• Experience coordinating complex diligence processes across multiple stakeholders
• Track record of excellence within investment banking and strong academic foundation
• Pursuing / completed additional financial certifications such as CFA, FRM 
• Proficiency with AI/LLM tools and workflows to enhance research, drafting, and analytical tasks is preferred
ABOUT US
JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.
We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.
About The Team
J.P. Morgan's Commercial & Investment Bank is a global leader across banking, markets, securities services and payments. Corporations, governments and institutions throughout the world entrust us with their business in more than 100 countries. The Commercial & Investment Bank provides strategic advice, raises capital, manages risk and extends liquidity in markets around the world.

• Exceptional financial and valuation modeling skills

• Monitor CMA regulatory announcements, corporate actions, rights issues, and IPO pipeline relevant to covered sectors.

title: Investment Analyst, Portfolio Management
description:
ABOUT VANTROCK
Vantrock is an operator-led real assets platform, built to work in the white space of every strategy it enters. A real asset is three jobs: finding the land, building and running the asset, managing the capital that owns it. Vantrock does all three with one team. Headquartered in Mumbai, it originates, develops, operates and manages institutional-grade real assets from land to operations. Warehousing, industrial and logistics parks are the first strategy. The platform is run by operators, and it is built to run lean. Suburban office campuses, strata offices, data centres, senior living and infrastructure assets follow, each as its own strategy, sequenced on delivery and each in a white space others have left open, with a clear path to REITs and InvITs. Real assets only, across every class the platform grows into, in sequence.
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
The portfolio management company needs clean research, accurate data and books that close every day. This seat provides all three, working directly with the Principal Officer.
It is an analyst seat with a wide view. You research listed markets and credit, build the real asset data that sits behind the platform's thinking, and keep the portfolios, records and reports right. You prepare the case. The Principal Officer makes the decision.
You should not apply if you want a pure research seat with no reconciliation in it. The operations work is half the seat, and it matters as much as the research.
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
• Conduct research and analysis on listed companies to identify potential investment opportunities.
• Analyse financial statements, business performance, earnings growth, balance sheets and cash flows.
• Assist in preparing financial models, company valuations, investment notes and research reports.
• Track stock-market developments, company announcements, quarterly results and relevant sector trends.
• Monitor portfolio holdings, share-price movements, investment performance and sector exposures.
• Support portfolio reviews, investment recommendations and periodic reporting.
• Research real estate industry fundamentals, including property demand, rental growth, REIT performance, developer sales and leverage.
• Maintain investment research records and supporting documentation.
• Coordinate with the investment team to support portfolio monitoring and other investment-related activities.
• Follow applicable internal policies, investment mandates and regulatory procedures.
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Essential
• A graduate degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian or foreign university.
• 2+ years in the securities market, at a portfolio manager, alternative investment manager, asset manager, stock broker, investment adviser or research analyst. Real estate development, leasing or consulting does not count towards this.
• Excel models you have built yourself.
• You use AI tools every day in your work and can show what you have done with them.
• Mumbai, on site.
Advantageous
• An MBA, a CA, or the CFA at any level.
• NISM certifications, such as XXI-B or XIX-D.
• Real estate or infrastructure investing, REITs or InvITs.
• Bloomberg, Capitaline, ACE Equity or similar tools.
• Portfolio accounting or back-office systems.
What this role is not
• It is not a decision-making seat. You do not approve investments or vote at the Investment Committee.
• It is not an investment banking seat. Deal preparation and investor coordination for the platform sit with the capital formation team.
• It is not a finance or accounts seat. Accounts and treasury sit with the finance team.
STANDING REQUIREMENTS
AI proficiency is a standing requirement in every seat at Vantrock. You use AI tools daily as force multipliers, and you judge their output rather than forwarding it. This is tested for every appointment through a supervised assessment. There are no exceptions by seniority.
Partner command is the second standing requirement. Vantrock runs on outsourced partners, so every person here must be able to scope, brief, hold to an SLA, score and commercially discipline a partner, and must know what should never be delegated.
COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY
The people who build the platform own a piece of it, vesting over time. A market salary covers the month. The rest of what you earn here is built: pay on what you bring in, for land, leases and capital, so a good year in your seat is yours and not only the company's, and a stake in a platform designed to be worth more for every rupee it manages than one assembled the old way. Most careers in this industry pay you for your time. This one is built to make you wealthier for what you build. Run your seat like it is yours, because part of it is.
CULTURAL FIT
We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
We don't fill seats. We build the platform.

title: Corporate & Investment Banking Credit Risk Analyst
description:
Job Description
Are you looking for an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and growing team in a fast paced and challenging area? This is a unique opportunity for you to work in our team to partner with the Business to provide a comprehensive view.
As a Wholesale Credit Risk APAC – Analyst in the Wholesale Credit Risk APAC team, you will be based in Mumbai playing a crucial role in onboarding new clients, performing credit analysis, structuring, negotiating, and developing recommendations for new transaction approvals across a variety of products, including loans, derivatives, and treasury products. You will lead due diligence and credit analysis to assess the creditworthiness of counterparties, making recommendations on appropriate structures, risk appetite, and client grading. Your role will involve ongoing credit risk portfolio management, new client onboardings, portfolio reviews and ad-hoc macro environment related stress exercises. You will also be committed to personal development and fostering team knowledge by coaching and training members of the Analyst community. Your ability to balance a commercial mindset with a sound risk and controls attitude will be key to managing the Firm's balance sheet effectively.
Job Responsibilities
• Demonstrate proactive ownership of your assigned portfolio of clients including borrower/market performance and acting as the main point of contact for all internal and external stakeholders for your portfolio
• Conduct transaction due diligence and credit analysis to assess counterparty creditworthiness
• Make recommendations on appropriate structure, risk appetite, and client grading informed by forward-looking credit analysis
• Participate in structuring and documentation negotiations with the support of senior colleagues
• Balance a commercial and solution-driven mindset with a sound risk and controls attitude
• Commit to personal development and foster team knowledge through coaching and training
• Develop close working relationships with various stakeholders/product partners within the Commercial & Investment Bank
• Drive key initiatives and process changes by identifying limitations/gaps in systems, risk controls, and policies
Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills
• Bachelor's Degree in Business, Finance, or a related field
• Familiarity with the concepts of Credit Risk – how it may arise and potential mitigants
• Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to establish credibility and trust with internal business and risk stakeholders
• Ability to demonstrate good time management and clarity in thinking when dealing with multiple work streams in a fast-paced environment
• Ability to think holistically and logically and communicate own views in an easy to understand fashion
Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills
• 2-3 years of experience in credit risk management in the financial services industry would be highly regarded
• Relevant postgraduate qualifications (e.g., MBA, Masters of Finance, CFA, CA) would be highly regarded
• Knowledge of the Corporates and Financial Institutions financial analysis

description:
The Global Leveraged Finance Underwriting Credit Team (“LFU”) within Institutional Credit Management (“ICM”) is seeking an Snr Analyst to join its Analytics team. The Snr Analyst is a professional with the goal to deliver best-in-class credit risk analysis, monitoring and credit administration as a partner to broader ICM Underwriting and Banking, Capital Markets and Advisory’s (BCMA) shared commitment to ensuring the safety and soundness of wholesale lending across ICG. The Snr Analyst will work with the rest of the LFU team to create a best-in-class Leveraged Lending Underwriting organization with the primary goal of materially enhancing Citi’s end-to-end Leveraged Lending credit management process.

• Monitor the covered portfolio, including following industry trends, impacts to key relationships, and escalation of potential credit issues to LFU Underwriters, Risk and BCMA partners
• Evaluate and gain a strong understanding of clients' business model, financial performance, and key credit drivers across various industries, through both due diligence process as part of transactions and ongoing credit monitoring responsibilities
• Assess the borrower’s cash flow profile by building projection models used in assigning a regulatory rating and driving decision on the extension of credit to highly levered obligors
• Provide analytical support across LFU’s core functions: (1) Leveraged Lending transaction origination and credit approval; (2) portfolio management and early problem recognition; (3) global leveraged lending related projects and strategic initiatives

title: Senior Analyst-Risk Management
description:
Job Description
Overview of The Department
Commercial Rating and Underwriting (CRU) sits within the Credit and Fraud Risk (CFR) division and forms the institutional credit risk management function within American Express. The CRU team plays the critical role of assessing and managing the risk of institutional exposures across all business units within American Express, and in all regions globally. Credit exposures are primarily generated through corporate and small business card programs, via merchant service relationships where non-delivery risk exists, and among the securities portfolio held for firm-wide liquidity. CRU is led from Salt Lake City with regional teams in New York, London, Singapore , Sydney and India.
In addition to determining the internal credit rating which drives the probability of default of each exposure, CRU also calculates the loss given default of these obligors while underwriting card programs. As a bank holding company, American Express must comply with the highest global banking standards set by Basel and implemented by the bank’s primarily regulatory, the Federal Reserve.
Responsibilities
Job Responsibilities
Analyst will be based out of India, and responsible for rating and underwriting credit exposures predominantly for English speaking market,. Fundamental analysis incorporates a thorough review of business, financial, industry and country risk coupled with support from internal and external rating model outputs. Assessment includes understanding of the need for credit extension, profitability of the relationship and program structures.
Analysts will have opportunity to interact with various teams across the firm including front office sales, business unit risk partners, and credit administration to perform their critical role.
Desired Skills
•  Experience as a credit analyst or underwriter dealing with commercial exposures ranging from small business or middle-market to large, multinational institutions 
•  Thorough understanding of fundamental financial analysis including the ability to review corporate financial statements to determine the ability of the obligor to honor its credit obligations 
•  Comfort with GAAP/IFRS accounting standards, corporate valuation, and forecasting 
•  Familiarity with quantitative credit models (such as Moody’s RiskCalc, CreditEdge, etc) and knowledge of how to interpret the outputs, and when deviation from the model has appropriate defense 
•  Comfort with public agency ratings and supporting analysis 
•  Understanding of current macroeconomic trends and how to provide recommendations to improve the PD estimation based on the business cycle 
•  Experience preparing company-specific and industry-wide credit memorandums 
•  Familiarity with global markets (foreign language ability a plus) 
Qualifications
 QUALIFICATIONS 
•  3-4 years experience rating and / or underwriting at a leading financial institution or rating agency 
•  Bachelor’s degree from a top tier university with high GPA and a degree (or substantial coursework) in finance, accounting, economics, or statistics 
•  Chartered Financial Analyst program candidacy a plus 
About Us
At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.
As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career. Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

We back you with benefits that support your holistic well-being so you can be and deliver your best. This means caring for you and your loved ones' physical, financial, and mental health, as well as providing the flexibility you need to thrive personally and professionally:

description:
FC Global Services India LLP (First Citizens India), a part of First Citizens BancShares, Inc., a top 20 U.S. financial institution, is a global capability center (GCC) based in Bengaluru. Our India-based teams benefit from the company’s over 125-year legacy of strength and stability. First Citizens India is responsible for delivering value and managing risks for our lines of business. We are particularly proud of our strong, relationship-driven culture and our long-term approach, which are deeply ingrained in our talented workforce. This is evident across all key areas of our operations, including Technology, Enterprise Operations, Finance, Cybersecurity, Risk Management, and Credit Administration. We are seeking talented individuals to join us in our mission of providing solutions fit for our clients’ greatest ambitions.
Job Description
Value Proposition
At First Citizens India, you’ll have the opportunity to be more than just an analyst, you’ll be a trusted partner in safeguarding the Bank’s credit portfolio.
• Global Exposure: Collaborate directly with Senior Credit and Risk professionals in the U.S., gaining insights into global credit practices.
• Impactful Work: Play a critical role in monitoring a multi-billion-dollar credit portfolio, helping the Bank stay resilient and client-centric.
• Career Growth: Build your expertise in Credit analysis while having access to structured learning, mentorship, and opportunities to move into leadership roles.
• Innovation at Scale: Be part of a team driving process improvement and technology adoption in Credit monitoring.
• Culture of Stability & Growth: Join a Bank that has thrived for over 125 years, balancing stability with continuous growth and innovation.
Job Details
• Position Title: Senior Analyst, Credit Analysis
• Career Level: P2
• Job Category: Senior Associate
• Role Type: Hybrid
• Job Location: Bengaluru, Karnataka
About the Team: Credit Analysis
We are a diverse and highly skilled team of Credit professionals, experienced in Origination, Underwriting, and end-to-end Portfolio Monitoring.
Our team specializes in Technology & Healthcare Accelerator & Growth, Corporate Banking, Sponsor Finance, Fund Banking, Commercial Real Estate (CRE), Healthcare – Medical Office Building (MOB), Wine, Community Assistance Banking (CAB), and Community Development Finance (CDF) loans monitoring across Innovation Banking, Fund Banking, Commercial Finance and General Bank. Additionally, the team supports the Centralized Cash Management Team (CCMT). Team works closely with US-based Credit Solutions team, Credit Officers, and Portfolio Managers to perform monthly, quarterly & annual monitoring of the loans.
Impact
As a Senior Analyst in the Credit Analysis team at First Citizens India, you will play a pivotal role in safeguarding the Bank’s credit quality and supporting informed lending decisions. This role is critical to enabling the Bank to make confident lending decisions, manage risks effectively, and maintain trusted relationships with clients. In this role, you will Leverage tools such as Moody’s Credit Lens, and other commercial lending platforms to deliver accurate, timely, and actionable insights.
You’ll Partner with Global Credit teams to ensure Risk management and strengthen Portfolio performance.
Key Deliverables
As a Senior Analyst – Credit Analysis, you will play a critical role in supporting the ongoing management of Bank’s Credit portfolio. You will work closely with U.S. based Credit Officers, Portfolio Managers, and other stakeholders to deliver high-quality analysis and monitoring insights that help safeguard the Bank’s Credit exposure while ensuring client success.
General Functions May Include, But Are Not Limited To
• Credit Portfolio Monitoring: Support ongoing monitoring of assigned credit portfolio to identify potential risks and ensure compliance with Loan agreement and risk policies.
• Reporting Tasks Monitoring: Monitor and track monthly/quarterly reporting packages (arriving from US counterparts) to check for completeness of client information on the portal.
• New Client Addition and Modification: Set up/upload new client information in the portal in tune with Loan Security Agreement; monitor and update the modifications in the portal in accordance with Loan Modification Agreements.
• Financial Spreading & Analysis: Spread and analyze financial statements of borrowers in Moody’s CreditLens, identifying key trends, risks, and opportunities.
• Covenant Monitoring: Track borrower compliance with financial and non-financial covenants, raising early alerts on potential breaches.
• Borrowing Base Calculations: Perform accurate and timely borrowing base calculations, ensuring alignment with loan documentation and lending practices.
• Reporting & MI: Prepare recurring and ad-hoc reports to provide insights into portfolio performance, sectoral trends, and emerging risks.
• Risk Alerts & Escalations: Support early identification of problem credits through financial deterioration, covenant breaches, or industry headwinds.
• Collaboration: Partner with U.S. stakeholders across Credit, and Operations to ensure consistent standards, accuracy, and timeliness in deliverables.
• Process Improvement: Contribute ideas to enhance automation, standardization, and efficiency in portfolio monitoring processes.
• Quality Assurance: Ensure high level of accuracy in performance of all tasks. Adhere to reporting, financial spreading and covenant calculation KPIs/metrics, completing work within agreed to turnaround times. Report incidents of non-compliance items (e.g., differences in financial statements provided by client) to lead analyst/manager on a timely basis.
• Mentoring juniors: Monitor tasks to be completed by other team members and support the manager in mentoring and training of new hire analysts.
Skills And Qualification
Functional Skills:
• Hands-on experience in spreading, covenant monitoring, and credit reporting.
• Strong knowledge of corporate lending products, credit documentation, and financial statement analysis.
• Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to work independently while being an active team contributor.
• Efficient and well organized, able to work under tight deadlines
• Outstanding attention to detail, accuracy, and ability to multitask
• Ability to be flexible with shift timings (2 pm – 11 pm)
Technical Skills
• Bachelor’s degree in Commerce / MBA(Finance).
• Chartered Accountant / CFA / equivalent qualifications will be an added advantage.
• Experience: 3–5 years of experience in credit analysis, portfolio monitoring in a bank, NBFC, or financial services firm.
• Exposure to US accounting, GAAP, and IFRS
• Proficiency in MS Excel and financial analysis tools; familiarity with SQL, Power BI, Tableau is an advantage.
Leadership Qualities
• This is an individual contributor role; however, the role may require adhoc workflow management/ supporting team leaders/managers as warranted.
• High level of ownership and self-drive towards proactive portfolio risk management
• High on Self-management and situational leadership
Relationships & Collaboration
This role involves working with the Credit Analysis team, reporting to the Credit Analysis Manager. This role will have comprehensive training across credit analysis processes, owning and managing an independent portfolio and collaboration with the lending team and other stakeholders. This role also requires strong communication, and teamwork skills are essential.

title: Manager-Risk Management
description:
Job Description
Overview of The Department
Commercial Rating and Underwriting (CRU) sits within the Credit and Fraud Risk (CFR) division and forms the institutional credit risk management function within American Express. The CRU team plays the critical role of assessing and managing the risk of institutional exposures across all business units within American Express, and in all regions globally.Credit exposures are primarily generated through corporate and small business card programs, via merchant service relationships where non-delivery risk exists, and among the securities portfolio held for firm-wide liquidity.CRU is led from Salt Lake City with regional teams in New York, London, Singapore , Sydney and India.
In addition to determining the internal credit rating which drives the probability of default of each exposure, CRU also calculates the loss given default of these obligors while underwriting card programs. As a bank holding company, American Express must comply with the highest global banking standards set by Basel and implemented by the bank’s primarily regulatory, the Federal Reserve.
Responsibilities
Job Responsibilities
The CRU Manager is responsible for independently determining credit rating of mid and large corporate borrowers across diversified industries through fundamental analysis, along with underwriting credit exposures. While fundamental analysis incorporates a thorough review of industry, business, financial and country risk coupled with support from internal and external rating model outputs, credit underwriting includes understanding the need for credit extension, profitability of the relationship and program structures.
Responsibilities
Role will involve ongoing management and continuous monitoring of portfolio hygiene as well as conducting research and analysis to develop industry/sector expertise and knowledge. Further responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:
• Managing the team workflow and ensure timely completion of assigned activities and maintaining the productivity standards of the team,
• Ensure accuracy of underwriting decisions for himself/herself and the team 
• Leading analyst(s) on Coaching & Development, Performance Management, Evaluation and Monitoring
• Attend internal and external stakeholders’ meetings where appropriate to support business outcomes. 
• Be current on all firm-wide risk policies and ensure all governance, reporting and data quality requirements are met and maintained for borrowers and borrower groups,
Qualifications
Past Experience 
5-8 years with relevant experience gained in Corporate Credit & Risk Management function of a Corporate or Institutional Bank with minimum 3 years of experience as an approving authority and people leader.
Academic Background 
• MBA from Top Tier B-School or professional qualification in Accountancy, 
• Professional qualifications like Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and/or Financial Risk Manager (FRM), is a plus
Functional/ Technical Skills
• Robust understanding of Financial Statements including Ratio Analysis, Cash Flow Analysis, Accounting Standards, Accounting treatment and Financial Adjustments 
• Clear grasp of Corporate Finance concepts and their application
About Us
At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.
As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career. Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

title: Senior Analyst
description:
Job Summary 
The individual will support the Corporate Banking credit teams in conducting comprehensive annual reviews of corporate borrowers. The role involves detailed financial statement analysis, credit risk assessment, industry research, monitoring portfolio performance, and evaluating ongoing borrower creditworthiness to support lending and risk management decisions.
Key Responsibilities 
• Conduct annual credit reviews for corporate banking clients across various industries and borrower segments.
• Analyze historical and projected financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, cash flow statements, and key credit metrics.
• Assess borrower performance, liquidity, leverage, cash flow generation, debt servicing capacity, and overall financial health.
• Perform detailed ratio analysis, trend analysis, and peer benchmarking to identify strengths, risks, and emerging credit concerns.
• Review compliance with financial covenants, reporting requirements, and credit policy guidelines.
• Evaluate business performance, management strategy, market position, industry dynamics, and macroeconomic factors impacting credit quality.
• Prepare comprehensive annual review credit memoranda, including borrower overview, risk assessment, financial analysis, covenant review, and recommendation of internal risk ratings.
Required Qualifications 
• Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or related field.
• Strong understanding of corporate banking, commercial lending, and credit risk principles.
• Experience analyzing financial statements and assessing borrower creditworthiness.
• Knowledge of credit metrics such as Debt/EBITDA, Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio (FCCR), Interest Coverage Ratio, leverage, liquidity, and cash flow measures.
• Familiarity with corporate credit documentation, covenant structures, and risk rating methodologies.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and financial analysis tools.
• Strong analytical, written, and communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple reviews and deliver within strict timelines.

title: Senior Industry Research Analyst
description:
Job Requirements

The Senior Industry Research Analyst will support the Wholesale Banking Risk function by delivering deep, sector-agnostic insights across high-exposure industries in the bank’s portfolio. •  Stay updated with market intelligence through peer networking and industry publications.

Education

•  Excellent research and analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex industry data
•  Strong understanding of macroeconomic and sectoral trends

•  Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams

title: Financing & Risk Solutions Analyst
description:
Join us as a Financing & Risk Solutions Analyst
•  In this crucial role, you'll support the Specialty Finance desk in delivering high-quality monitoring, analysis and risk oversight across securitisation transactions, including consumer loans, credit cards, auto loans and other structured finance products
•  You'll play a key role in overseeing AUP processes, reviewing IPD waterfall reports and assessing ongoing transaction performance to support effective risk management and decision-making
•  This is a fantastic opportunity to build specialist expertise in structured finance, supported by training, self-development opportunities and exposure to a broad range of transactions and stakeholders
•  We’re offering this role at senior analyst level
What you’ll do
As a Financing & Risk Solutions Analyst, you'll support the effective management of securitisation transactions, ensuring activities remain aligned to the bank's conduct, operational, credit and regulatory risk frameworks. You'll help monitor transaction performance, analyse key risks and support the ongoing oversight of complex structured finance portfolios.
We'll also look to you to prepare analysis, presentations, reviews and supporting documentation that contribute to origination and portfolio management activities. You'll work closely with client coverage teams and a wide range of internal stakeholders, helping deliver insight that supports informed decision-making and strong customer outcomes.
Your Day-to-day Activities Will Include
•  Preparing investor presentations, market analysis and other marketing materials, while monitoring market developments and identifying emerging trends and opportunities
•  Supporting the preparation of corporate finance advisory materials and financial models across the US technology sector
•  Monitoring US and European debt markets, producing market updates across investment grade, high yield and leveraged loan markets
•  Writing market commentary for clients and maintaining internal databases covering issuance activity, investor demand, pricing analysis and transaction performance
•  Analysing financial performance and preparing peer comparison analysis, including spread, yield and relative value assessments to support transaction and investment discussions
The skills you'll need
To succeed in this role, you'll hold an MBA in Finance or a professional qualification such as CA, CFA or FRM. You'll also bring a strong understanding of financial markets, structured finance products and financial statement analysis, together with experience using industry-standard platforms such as Bloomberg, Intex, Reuters, FactSet and Dealogic.
We're looking for someone with strong experience in securitisation, structured credit or portfolio monitoring, ideally gained within an investment banking, capital markets or analytical risk environment.
You’ll Also Demonstrate
•  Experience working within cash management, fixed income, investment banking or credit research functions supporting debt-related products and transactions
•  A good understanding of investment banking products, credit markets and structured finance solutions
•  Strong analytical capabilities, including ratio analysis, sector assessment, pitch book preparation and financial modelling
•  Excellent numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex information and deliver clear, insightful analysis

title: Credit Analyst
description:
Opening for Investment Banking client.
The individual will be responsible for credit analysis of existing or new financial institution clients/counterparties. Day-to-day responsibilities include:
• Assessing the creditworthiness of counterparties: prepare detailed credit application by capturing relevant information as per internal policies, perform credit outlooks, recommend risk ratings using bank’s internal rating tools, and propose global credit limits based on internal risk appetite.

title: Mgr. Supply Chain Planning & Logistics
description:
Company Description
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
Job Description
Primary Function of the Position
We are seeking a supply chain professional to own end-to-end demand forecasting, supply planning, inventory control, and logistics execution for a portfolio of medical devices — capital equipment, instruments, accessories, and spare parts.
The role drives a disciplined S&OP process across a regulated, lot-traceable, and often import-dependent supply chain — balancing patient-facing service levels, working capital, regulatory compliance, and cost-to-serve.
The incumbent will be the bridge between Commercial (tender + commercial channel), Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Manufacturing / Imports, Finance, and Service — ensuring on-shelf availability of life-critical products and uninterrupted service support to the installed base.
Key Responsibilities
Demand Planning & Forecast Management
• Own statistical and consensus demand forecasts at SKU / region / channel level, segmented by capital equipment, instruments, accessories, consumables, and spares, on a rolling 18-month horizon.
• Support New Product Introduction (NPI) launches — build phase-in plans aligned to regulatory milestones, sales-force readiness, and channel fill.
• Manage EOL and product-transition planning with care — clinical preferences and regulatory constraints make abrupt phase-outs risky.
• Run spare-parts and accessory planning driven by installed-base data, attach rates, and service-event history.
• Track forecast accuracy — MAPE, WMAPE, bias, FVA — at category level; isolate tender forecast error from commercial baseline.
Supply Planning & Inventory Control
• Convert the demand plan into a constrained supply plan across in-house.
• Work closely with global Supply planner.
• Own inventory planning and control — safety stock, cycle stock, and strategic stock — segmented by criticality (lifesaving / Class C-D items held at higher service levels, slow-moving accessories at lower tier).
• Manage expiry, FEFO discipline, and inventory ageing to keep write-offs within target.
• Plan around import lead times, CDSCO license validity, and customs clearance dependencies for imported SKUs.
• Coordinate with global stakeholders — regional supply hubs, principal manufacturers, and global category / planning teams — for supply allocation, expedites, and execution tracking across time zones.
Logistics & Service Levels
• Oversee inbound (imports + domestic), inter-DC, and outbound logistics to distributors, hospitals (direct), and field service engineers.
• Manage 3PL/4PL partners under ISO 13485-aligned vendor audits and Good Distribution Practices (GDP).
• Track and improve OTIF, lane-level cold-chain excursion %, expiry write-off %, freight cost per unit, OTIF-to-hospital direct, and tender-fulfilment %.
S&OP & Stakeholder Integration
• Run a disciplined monthly S&OP — Demand Review → Supply Review → Pre-S&OP → Executive S&OP — with a separate tender pipeline review layered in.
• Act as the single integrator across Commercial, Tender, Service, Regulatory, Quality, Manufacturing, Imports, and Finance; quantify trade-offs (service to a hospital vs. expiry risk vs. cash).
• Drive scenario plans for tender wins/losses, NPI go-live shifts, supplier disruptions, and import delays.
Analytics, Systems & Continuous Improvement
• Drive deployment and adoption of planning systems — o9, SAP — alongside QMS-integrated traceability in ERP.
• Build dashboards for forecast accuracy, inventory ageing / expiry runway, service level by hospital, tender OTIF, and import lead-time variance.
• Champion Lean / Six Sigma initiatives and GDP-aligned SOPs; institutionalize a logistics control tower for critical SKUs.
Stakeholder Management
• Manage cross functional stakeholders across commercial, Service, Regulatory, Manufacturing, Planning , Imports and Finance.
• Build and sustain Strong working relationship with global counterparts ,3PL/4PL Partners.
• Represent the function in senior business reviews and external audits (CDSCO, ISO 13485 surveillance).
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
• 7–10 years of professional experience in a similar position, ideally within a medical device company.
• Demonstrated ownership of demand planning, supply planning, and logistics in a regulated, multi-channel environment.
• Strong analytical skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
• Strong communication skills, both verbal and written.
• Effective time management and ability to drive multiple parallel workstreams.
• Ability to build and sustain long-term professional relationships across cross-functional and external stakeholders.
Required Education And Training
• Bachelor's degree (Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or related discipline).
Preferred Skills And Experience
• MBA / PGDM in Operations or Supply Chain Management.
• Familiarity with an integrated ERP, preferably SAP (MM / SD / PP modules).
• Hands-on exposure to advanced planning systems — o9,SAP
• Strong knowledge of the MS Office product suite, particularly Excel (advanced functions, Power Query).
• Working knowledge of CDSCO Medical Devices Rules 2017, GDP, and ISO 13485 as applied to distribution and storage.
• APICS CPIM / CSCP / CLTD or Lean Six Sigma certification.
• Exposure to Power BI / Tableau for analytics and dashboard
Additional Information

You will build a reliable and traceable supply base, keep BOM cost and lead times under control, and protect research and production from shortages and obsolescence. You will lead a team of procurement, planning and supplier quality specialists and use data to show what is working. 
Are you ready to be part of a dynamic, fast-growing team? If yes, then let’s solve the real problems and innovate newer possibilities. Sounds interesting? Come, join us on this incredible journey!
Don’t just dream about what’s next – build it!
Essential Skills:

• Strong working knowledge of authorised-distribution channels (DigiKey, Mouser, Arrow, Avnet and franchised local partners), and of when and how to quote direct with a manufacturer. 
• Experience in traceability and counterfeit avoidance: franchised sourcing, certificates of conformance and control of broker purchases. 
• Ability to cost a full BOM at build quantities and flag long-lead, single-source and end-of life lines.

• • Background in aerospace, defence, drone (UAS) or a related high-tech industry is a plus.

• Identify single-source, allocation and end-of-life risks, and set up dual sourcing and last time buys before a disruption. 
• Drive supplier scorecards, performance reviews and corrective-action plans with electronics suppliers. 
• Share meaningful insights with leadership, such as savings, lead-time trends, shortages and supplier performance. 
• Lead and develop a team of electronics procurement, planning and supplier quality specialists. 
• Document what is learned about parts, suppliers and systems so the next person starts faster.

• MBA in Operations / Supply Chain is a plus. 
• 6–10 years of experience in electronics procurement or supply chain, with at least 2 years leading a team.

title: Planning Lead
description:
Role purpose
The Planning Manager leads end-to-end demand, supply, production and inventory planning for the Vision Care business. The role ensures reliable product availability, optimized inventory and efficient use of manufacturing and distribution capacity while balancing customer service, cost and working-capital objectives.
Key responsibilities
1. Sales and operations planning
•Lead the monthly S&OP/IBP cycle across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Manufacturing, Procurement and Logistics.
•Consolidate demand, capacity, supply, inventory and financial plans.
•Identify gaps and scenarios and facilitate management decisions.
•Maintain one agreed operational plan and track actions from planning reviews.
•Translate annual business plans into monthly and weekly operational plans.
2. Demand planning
•Lead statistical forecasting and market-input collection for lenses, coatings, consumables and related products.
•Review historical sales, seasonality, promotions, launches, tenders and customer trends.
•Challenge assumptions and resolve differences between commercial forecasts and statistical demand.
•Manage forecast accuracy and bias by product family, channel and region.
•Establish planning approaches for new products, phase-outs and intermittent demand.
3. Supply and production/Import planning
•Develop feasible supply and production plans across Import/Local plants, laboratories, distribution centers and external suppliers.
•Balance demand against material, machine, labor and supplier capacity.
•Set production priorities and manage bottlenecks, shortages and backlog.
•Coordinate make-to-stock, make-to-order and prescription-lens requirements.
•Ensure timely escalation of supply risks with clear recovery plans.
• Work with Procurement on supplier constraints, lead times and material availability.
4. Inventory management
• Define inventory targets, safety stocks, reorder parameters and segmentation policies.
• Optimize inventory across raw materials, semi-finished lenses, finished goods and consumables.
• Monitor ageing, slow-moving and obsolete inventory.
• Coordinate mitigation actions for excess stock and expiry or obsolescence risks.
• Improve working capital without compromising agreed service levels.
5. Product lifecycle and launch planning
• Lead supply-chain readiness for new products, coatings, technologies and portfolio changes.
• Coordinate demand ramp-up, material availability, production validation and initial stock.
• Manage end-of-life transitions and depletion of discontinued materials.
• Minimize write-offs and customer-service disruption during portfolio transitions.
6. Customer-service and exception management
• Monitor fill rate, order fulfilment, backorders and delivery performance.
• Lead cross-functional response to major shortages and demand changes.
• Prioritize constrained supply using agreed commercial and customer-service rules.
• Communicate recovery dates, risks and alternatives to relevant stakeholders.
7. Systems, data and process improvement
• Ensure accurate planning parameters and master data in SAP and associated planning tools.
• Drive planning automation, analytics and process standardization.
• Improve forecast models, planning horizons, frozen periods and exception-management rules.
• Support ERP, APS, IBP and digital supply-chain initiatives.
• Maintain planning documentation, controls and audit readiness.
8. Team leadership
• Build analytical, commercial and supply-chain capabilities within the team.
• Promote fact-based decisions, accountability and cross-functional collaboration.
• Establish succession and competency-development plans.
Key performance indicators
• Forecast accuracy and forecast bias
• Customer service level, OTIF and fill rate
• Production-plan adherence
• Inventory value, days of inventory and inventory turns
• Slow-moving and obsolete inventory
• Backorder value and ageing
• Capacity utilization
• Planning master-data accuracy
• S&OP action closure and decision quality
• Working capital and logistics-expedite/Diversion costs
Qualifications
•Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Operations, Engineering (STEM background mandatory).
•Master’s degree or MBA is advantageous.
•APICS CPIM/CSCP, IBF or equivalent certification is advantageous.
•Typically, 6-8 years of supply-chain experience, including at least 4 years in a planning role in handling complex SKU portfolio handling and assortment planning
•Experience in medical technology, optical products, healthcare, precision manufacturing or consumer goods is desirable.
Technical competencies
•Strong knowledge of demand, supply, production and inventory planning.
•Practical experience with S&OP or IBP processes.
•Advanced SAP experience, ideally including SD, MM, PP and APO/IBP.
•Strong Excel and data-analysis capabilities; Power BI or similar tools are advantageous.
•Understanding of MRP, capacity planning, safety stock and product lifecycle management.
•Ability to analyze complex product portfolios with short lead-time and customized-order requirements.
•Familiarity with Lean, continuous improvement and root-cause analysis.
•Leadership and behavioral competencies
•Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills.
•Ability to influence senior stakeholders without direct authority.
•Clear communication and effective meeting facilitation.
• Customer-focused and commercially aware decision-making.
• Confidence in managing ambiguity, constraints and competing priorities.
• Strong people leadership and coaching capability.
• High ownership, integrity and attention to detail.

title: Manager, Digital Supply Chain Implementation, PI - Global Capability Center
description:
Description

Firm & Practice Contribution
• Develop thought leadership, industry perspectives, benchmarks, and reusable tools / frameworks to strengthen the firm's Digital Supply Chain proposition

Qualifications
• 6-11 years of experience in digital supply chain transformation, supply chain planning, logistics, operations excellence, or digital supply chain technology implementation programs
• Previous advisory and consulting experience from a top-tier strategy firm, leading specialist / niche advisory firm, or Big-4 consultancy preferred
• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, logistics, supply chain, manufacturing or a related field

• Strong functional knowledge across the end-to-end supply chain, including demand & supply planning, manufacturing, procurement, production scheduling, inventory, logistics, distribution, and order fulfilment

• Hands-on experience with ERP and supply chain platforms such as SAP ECC/S4HANA, SAP IBP, SAP EWM/TM, Oracle SCM Cloud, Blue Yonder, Kinaxis, Microsoft Dynamics, o9, WMS / TMS or similar solutions

Your journey at A&M

title: Supply Chain Manager - Mechanical Procurement
description:
Supply Chain Manager – Mechanical Produrement
About the company:
Raphe mPhibr Pvt. Ltd is India’s largest R&D-driven UAV manufacturer, revolutionizing aerospace with indigenously developed, cutting-edge drone technology. Our UAVs have flown over 1 million kilometres across diverse terrains and weather conditions.
With 900+ talented professionals trained at premier institutions like MIT, Georgia Tech, IITs, and NITs and state-of-the-art research and manufacturing facilities, we design and build almost every component of our UAVs in-house. Our expertise spans Aerodynamics, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics, Software, and AI, enabling us to create comprehensive and customized end-to-end solutions.
Recognized for our rapid growth and inclusive culture, we were recently named LinkedIn's Top 10 Startups 2024 and honoured with the FICCI Women's Empowerment Award. Beyond work, we foster a collaborative, fun, and inclusive workplace, supported by unique events and thoughtful policies that reflect our commitment to our people We innovate for a better society!
We innovate for a better society!
Do you want? 
• The opportunity to work alongside highly innovative and technical minds?
• A competitive salary based on your skills?
• To make sure every UAV we build has the right mechanical parts, at a cost we can defend and on schedule?
Job Brief: 
We are looking for a Supply Chain Manager - Mechanical Procurement to own how Raphe sources, buys, plans and qualifies the mechanical raw materials and items that go into our products. You will build a capable international national supplier base, keep part and tooling costs defensible, and make sure material arrives at the required quality and on schedule. You will lead a team of procurement, sourcing and supplier quality specialists and use data to show what is working.
Are you ready to be part of a dynamic, fast-growing team? If yes, then let’s solve the real problems and innovate newer possibilities. Sounds interesting? Come, join us on this incredible journey!
Don’t just dream about what’s next – build it!
Essential Skills: 
• Experience sourcing mechanical raw materials and items.
• An established regional or national mechanical supplier network.
• Raw-material price tracking and long-term agreements for metal stock.
• Strong knowledge of materials and their cost drivers: aluminium alloys, steels, titanium, plastics and composites.
• Experience buying standard parts and hardware (fasteners, etc.) by specification with correct certifications.
• Strong negotiation and cost analysis skills: break a quotation into its cost drivers and challenge it with should-cost estimates.
• Experience qualifying and selecting suppliers on technical capability, capacity, quality system and delivery record.
• Experience with incoming inspection, nonconforming material and root cause and corrective action with suppliers.
• Experience in material planning: safety stock, reorder points and shortage management ranked by production impact.
• Team leadership skills, with the ability to coach and develop others.
Preferred Skills:
• Statistical and risk-based quality methods: measurement system analysis, acceptance sampling and critical characteristics.
• Category strategy built from spend analysis.
• Background in aerospace, defence, drone (UAS) or a related high-tech industry is a plus.
• Working knowledge of the processes behind the price: CNC machining, sheet metal, welding, casting, injection moulding, surface treatment and heat treatment.
As Supply Chain Manager - Mechanical Procurement, you will:
• Own the mechanical supply chain at Raphe, from supplier search to on-time delivery of every raw material
• Build and develop a global supplier base that delivers to specification, capacity, quality, cost and schedule.
• Maintain an approved mechanical supplier list with status, scope and open actions.
• Run RFQs, normalise quotations and negotiate price, payment terms and delivery schedule
• Negotiate long-term agreements for metal stock and other key raw materials.
• Maintain the Material Delivery Plan for mechanical parts and catch shortages before they hinder research or production.
• Ensure incoming inspections are performed on time to the right standards, and drive supplier corrective actions to closure.
• Identify single-source, capacity and sub-tier risks, and set up dual sourcing before a disruption.
• Share meaningful insights with leadership, such as savings, supplier scorecards, defect rates and shortages.
• Lead and develop a team of mechanical procurement, sourcing and supplier quality specialists.
• Document what is learned about parts, suppliers and systems so the next person starts faster.
Qualification and Experience:
• Bachelor’s degree preferably in Mechanical or related field.
• MBA in Operations / Supply Chain is a plus.
• 6–10 years of experience in mechanical procurement, sourcing or supply chain, with at least 2 years leading a team.

title: Supply Chain Manager
description:
Job Title: Supply Chain Manager – Finished Goods & Recycling Operations
Location: Nashik, Maharashtra (Plant)
Reports to: Director – Strategic Supply Chain, APAC
______________________________________________________________________________________________
Summary: Lead end-to-end supply chain operations for Electronica Tungsten Limited (ETL) in Nashik, an acquired company of Hyperion Materials & Technologies, while being employed under Hyperion payroll.
The role will oversee supply chain activities across ETL’s finished goods and recycling operations, including warehousing, transportation, direct sourcing of tungsten scrap and binder metals, Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP), import-export operations, licensing, and trade compliance supporting the recycling, production, and sale of WO₃, W, WC, and Ready-to-Press (RTP) powders.
The Supply Chain Manager will be responsible for ensuring the reliable, cost-effective, and fully compliant flow of materials across the end-to-end value chain, while developing a capable supply chain team and aligning ETL’s operations with Hyperion’s global supply chain and circularity strategy.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Warehouse Management
• Own finished goods and recycling-plant warehouse operations, including layout, storage of tungsten scrap, WO3/W/WC/RTP inventory, and hazardous/regulated material segregation as per statutory norms.
• Drive inventory accuracy, FIFO/batch traceability, cycle counts, and stock reconciliation between ERP/WMS and physical stock.
• Optimize warehouse capacity, layout, and material handling (5S, safety, and material-loss reduction) across all storage locations.
• Manage bonded/customs warehousing where applicable for imported scrap and export-bound finished goods.
Transportation Management
• Manage inbound transportation of tungsten scrap, cobalt, and nickel, and outbound distribution of finished goods (WO3, W, WC, RTP) to domestic and export customers.
• Select, negotiate, and manage 3PL/transporters and freight forwarders (road, rail, sea, and air) to optimize cost, transit time, and service levels.
• Ensure compliant transportation of hazardous and dual-use cargo, including correct documentation, packaging, and labelling. Track freight cost per ton/lane and drive continuous cost and lead-time optimization.
Direct Sourcing – Tungsten Scrap, Cobalt, Nickel
• Own direct sourcing of tungsten scrap (hard and soft), cobalt, nickel, and other binder metals to feed ETIL's recycling and manufacturing operations, in coordination with the global Sourcing & Procurement team.
• Develop and qualify domestic and international scrap and secondary-raw-material suppliers; build a resilient, diversified supply base in line with Hyperion's closed-loop circularity strategy.
• Track global tungsten, cobalt, and nickel price trends and indices to inform buy timing, pricing formulas, and landed-cost decisions.
• Negotiate long-term supply agreements and pricing terms for scrap and raw material inputs, balancing cost, quality, and supply continuity.
License Portfolio Management
• Own and maintain ETIL's complete import and export license portfolio required for recycling operations and sale of WO3, W, WC, and RTP, and for import of tungsten scrap.
• Manage the Importer-Exporter Code (IEC) and all associated DGFT authorizations, renewals, and amendments
• Obtain and renew hazardous/other-waste import authorizations from the State Pollution Control Board/CPCB and MoEF&CC (under the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules) for import of tungsten scrap and ensure Basel Convention documentation is for transboundary movement.
• Evaluate and manage SCOMET/dual-use export licensing obligations from DGFT applicable to tungsten and tungsten carbide products destined for controlled end-uses or end-users, including end-user certificates where required.
• Maintain licenses under EPR/consent-to-operate and other regulatory registrations relevant to recycling operations, and track renewal timelines to avoid lapses.
• Act as the primary liaison with DGFT, Customs, State Pollution Control Boards, MoEF&CC, and other regulatory authorities on licensing matters. Trade Compliance – Import and Export
• Ensure full compliance with India's Foreign Trade Policy, Customs Act, and applicable export-control regimes for all import of tungsten scrap/binder metals and export of finished tungsten products.
• Build and maintain internal trade-compliance controls: HS code classification, restricted-party/end-use screening, valuation, and documentation standards for every shipment.
• Coordinate with CHAs, freight forwarders, and Customs for smooth import/export clearance, and manage duty drawbacks, advance authorization, EPCG, or other applicable export-incentive schemes.
• Maintain audit-ready trade-compliance records and lead internal/external compliance audits and regulatory inspections.
• Monitor changes in DGFT notifications, SCOMET list updates, and hazardous-waste import policy, and proactively adapt ETIL's processes and licenses. Planning & S&OP
• Own the monthly Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) cycle, aligning demand forecasts, production plans, scrap/raw material availability, and finished goods inventory targets across Sales, Production, and Sourcing.
• Translate the S&OP plan into warehouse, transportation, and sourcing execution plans; monitor plan adherence and drive corrective action for gaps.
• Balance working-capital and inventory targets against service-level and supply-continuity requirements for both finished goods and recycling inputs.
• Provide supply chain inputs to budgeting, capacity planning, and new-business/product decisions.
Team Management
• Lead, develop, and manage the supply chain team across warehouse, logistics, sourcing, and trade compliance functions.
• Set goals, review performance, and build capability through training on regulatory, ERP, and process requirements.
• Foster a strong safety and compliance culture across warehouse and transportation operations.
• Partner cross-functionally with Production, Quality, Sales, Finance, and Legal to ensure the supply chain function supports ETIL's overall business goals.
Qualifications:
• Education: Graduate/Postgraduate in Supply Chain Management, Engineering (Metallurgy/Mechanical/Industrial), International Trade, or Business Administration; MBA or PG diploma in Supply Chain/Materials Management preferred.
• Experience: 10–15 years in supply chain, materials, or logistics management within metals, mining, recycling, or process manufacturing, with demonstrated ownership of import-export licensing and trade compliance; experience in the tungsten/carbide or non-ferrous metals recycling industry is a strong advantage.
• Skills Required: Warehouse and transportation management, S&OP process ownership, direct sourcing and negotiation, regulatory liaison and license management, team leadership, and analytical/ERP proficiency.
• Knowledge / Competencies: DGFT Foreign Trade Policy and IEC/SCOMET processes, Customs Act and import-export documentation, Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules and Basel Convention requirements, ERP (SAP/Oracle preferred), and working knowledge of the tungsten/carbide value chain.
Experience & Technical Skills:
• On-time-in-full (OTIF) delivery of finished goods to customers
• Warehouse inventory accuracy and space/capacity utilization
• Logistics/freight cost as a percentage of sales or cost per ton
• Zero compliance lapses, penalties, or shipment holds on import/export licenses and trade compliance
• License and authorization renewal turnaround time (100% on-time renewal)
• Tungsten scrap, cobalt, and nickel sourcing volume and cost vs. budget
• S&OP forecast accuracy and plan adherence
• Team capability, engagement, and safety performance

title: Manager, Supply Chain
description:
Imagine working at the forefront of innovation in fluid-flow technology, with over 1,400 colleagues across the globe, and contributing to a legacy of excellence that spans eight manufacturing facilities on four continents. Armstrong Fluid Technology is more than just a leader in our industry; we are a community of the brightest and most creative minds, driven by a shared mission to engineer the future and safeguard our planet.
As part of our team, you'll be immersed in an environment that fosters growth, creativity, and collaboration. Here, you'll have the opportunity to push boundaries, tackle exciting challenges, and develop cutting-edge solutions that promote energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact. Every day offers the chance to make a meaningful contribution to a more sustainable future, driving innovations that help lower global carbon footprints. Together, we’re creating a legacy that goes beyond business—one that’s changing the world for the better.
In this role, the Supply Chain Manager manages the supply chain team—driving procurement execution, material planning, and supplier performance to ensure on-time delivery, inventory optimization, and system efficiency, while developing people capabilities that support Armstrong’s operational excellence and customer satisfaction.
Key Accountabilities
Strategic & Analytical Thinking
• Forecasting demand and planning capacity while balancing cost, speed, and risk
• Making data-driven decisions using KPIs (inventory turnover, fill rate, lead time, OTIF)
• Seeing the end-to-end flow — not just their own link in the chain
• Adjusting to market shifts, tariffs, or supply shocks
• Driving continuous improvement (Lean, Six Sigma mindset)Financial Acumen
• Understanding cost structures — procurement, warehousing, transportation, inventory carrying costs
• Making trade-off decisions that protect margins without hurting service levels
Ensure On-Time Delivery (OTD) and Procurement Execution
• Drive on-time delivery (OTD) as a top-level KPI, aiming for high performance across all suppliers and value streams.
• Oversee timely procurement by ensuring buyers act on purchase requisitions promptly and in correct quantities & Focus on LT on deliveries
• Conduct daily shortage and backlog reviews with planners and buyers to ensure a continuous flow of production orders.
• Lead a daily cadence meeting with the entire buyer-planner team to review order releases, past dues (quantity and dollar value), and commodity-specific challenges.
• Monitor and support adherence to consignment agreements for critical parts such as castings and impellers sourced through partners like the Regional Supply Chain team.
Lead Material Planning and Inventory Optimization 
• Review Material Requirement Planning (MRP) signals regularly and coordinate material fulfillment by collaborating with suppliers and aggregating demand when feasible.
• Coordinate closely with global demand planners to align inventory and safety stock levels with forecasts.
• Optimize safety stock strategies, drive inventory turnover improvements, and enforce just-in-time (JIT) principles across Armstrong facilities and supplier sites.
• Lead efforts to improve forecasting precision and production order releases with internal planners, ensuring readiness aligned with capacity and customer expectations.
• Have CFT approach on new product launches and enhance material procurement plans accordingly.
Monitor and Improve Supply Chain Performance
• Develop and sustain delivery performance tracking systems using the PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) methodology to drive continuous improvement.
• Track and analyze key supply chain metrics such as lead times, order handling cycle times, and fill rates to enhance operational performance.
• Collaborate with customer service and sales teams to improve lead times and streamline the quote-to-fulfill cycle.
• Monitor global trends, disruptions, and risks to adapt supply chain strategies using tools like dual sourcing, supplier localization, and logistics optimization.
Strengthen Supplier Management and Accountability 
• Build and maintain strong supplier relationships through regular performance reviews, scorecards, and compliance checks.
• Conduct supplier audits and implement continuous improvement initiatives based on audit findings and operational KPIs.
• Collaborate with sourcing and supplier teams to proactively assess capacity constraints and implement delivery assurance strategies.
• Structure and assign supplier ownership clearly among buyers and planners by value streams, reducing overlap and improving accountability.
• Enforce ISO-compliant procedures for purchasing and planning functions to maintain quality and process integrity.
Lead and Develop Buyer-Planner Teams
• Supervise a team of buyer/planners categorized by product families and value streams.
• Clarify ownership of supplier portfolios by aligning responsibilities to specific value streams, reducing overlap and improving accountability.
• Drive transformation initiatives to realign team structure for better performance tracking and supplier relationship management.
• Conduct coaching, training, and performance reviews to build capability in ERP tools and supply chain analytics.
• Provide mentorship and day-to-day guidance to buyer-planners to improve performance and ownership.
Implement and Optimize Supply Chain Systems
• Lead the implementation of Kinaxis for advanced planning capabilities, guiding cross-functional teams through integration and change management.
• Monitor and correct LN ERP workflows and master data issues to ensure planning and execution systems are synchronized.
• Automate routine supply chain tasks and enhance system capabilities to improve forecast accuracy, planning responsiveness, and operational agility.
• Ensure that all systems are aligned to support dynamic planning requirements and real-time visibility into supply performance.
Integrate Supply Chain in New Products, Projects, and Regions
