title: Chief Of Staff And Strategic PMO - S And T
description:
At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.
Chief of Staff & Strategic PMO
The opportunity
As part of the GDS Strategy & Transformation function, the Chief of Staff & Strategic PMO will work closely with the GDS Strategy & Transformation Leader to translate strategic priorities into a focused and executable leadership agenda. The role will provide structured oversight across strategic priorities, transformation initiatives, leadership commitments and critical decision points, ensuring that the S&T Leader has the information, insights and follow-through required to drive the agenda effectively.
The role
We are looking for a seasoned Associate Director with 15+ years of experience who can operate at the intersection of strategy, executive leadership and execution. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct people-management responsibility.
The individual will act as a force multiplier to the GDS Strategy & Transformation Leader by bringing structure to complex priorities, anticipating leadership requirements, connecting interdependent initiatives and maintaining visibility of critical decisions, actions and risks. The successful candidate will be expected to understand business issues, challenge and synthesize information, and translate multiple workstreams into a coherent leadership view.
Your Key Responsibilities
• Partner closely with the GDS Strategy & Transformation Leader to structure and advance the function’s strategic and transformation agenda.
• Serve as a trusted thought partner to the GDS Strategy & Transformation Leader, helping shape leadership narratives, challenge assumptions, evaluate strategic alternatives and prepare for critical leadership discussions and decisions.
• Translate leadership priorities into clear workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, decision points and follow-through mechanisms.
• Maintain an integrated view of strategic priorities, leadership commitments and matters requiring intervention or decision.
• Anticipate upcoming leadership requirements and coordinate the analysis, materials and stakeholder inputs required for effective decision-making.
• Prepare executive briefings, leadership presentations, talking points, meeting materials and decision papers.
• Synthesize complex information from multiple teams into concise, leadership-ready narratives that highlight implications, risks, trade-offs, decisions required and next steps.
• Support preparation for critical leadership forums, ensuring consistency of storyline, facts and messages.
• Design and maintain the operating rhythm for the Strategy & Transformation function, including leadership reviews, portfolio and priority discussions, strategic planning cycles and executive decision forums. Define the purpose, cadence, participants, inputs and expected outcomes for each forum; coordinate agendas and pre-reads; ensure decisions, actions and accountabilities are clearly captured; and monitor follow-through, interdependencies and matters requiring escalation.
• Maintain an integrated portfolio view of strategic and transformation initiatives, including outcomes, milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions.
• Monitor execution against agreed priorities and proactively surface exceptions or areas requiring leadership attention.
• Drive disciplined closure of leadership actions and commitments across stakeholders.
• Identify dependencies and potential conflicts across workstreams and facilitate resolution with the relevant stakeholders.
• Develop concise dashboards and executive reporting focused on outcomes, exceptions and decisions rather than activity tracking.
• Assess whether strategic initiatives are progressing toward intended outcomes and surface emerging execution risks or opportunities.
• Act as a central coordination point across Strategy & Transformation and key GDS stakeholders, connecting teams where priorities are interdependent.
• Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across Service Lines and enabling functions and facilitate alignment where ownership spans multiple teams.
Skills And Attributes For Success
• Strong strategic and commercial judgement, with the ability to understand enterprise-level priorities and their implications.
• Excellent executive communication and advanced PowerPoint skills, including the ability to convert complex issues into crisp leadership narratives.
• Strong analytical capability and proficiency in Excel, with the ability to interrogate data and identify decision-relevant insights.
• Exceptional ability to connect the dots across multiple priorities, stakeholders and workstreams.
• Ability to distinguish matters requiring leadership attention from those that can be resolved at the working level.
• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, particularly when working with senior leaders without direct authority.
• Ability to challenge constructively while maintaining trusted relationships.
• High degree of ownership, judgement, discretion and confidentiality.
• Strong organizational discipline and ability to manage competing priorities without losing sight of strategic outcomes.
• Comfort working through ambiguity and changing leadership priorities with limited supervision.
To qualify for the role, you must have
• A minimum of 15 years of relevant professional experience, with significant exposure to strategy, transformation, business management, enterprise PMO, consulting, operations or leadership-office roles.
• An MBA or equivalent postgraduate qualification in business, strategy, finance, management or a related discipline
• Demonstrated experience working directly with or supporting senior executives and leadership teams.
• Experience coordinating complex, cross-functional strategic or transformation agendas.
• Strong experience developing executive presentations, leadership briefings and decision materials.
• Proven ability to drive outcomes through influence across stakeholders without direct reporting relationships.
• Strong analytical capabilities and advanced proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel.
• Experience overseeing governance, leadership actions, risks, dependencies and decision points across a portfolio of priorities.
• Demonstrated ability to move seamlessly between strategic thinking and execution discipline.
Ideally, you will also have
• Prior experience in a Chief of Staff, Strategy, Transformation, CEO/CXO Office, Business Management or enterprise PMO role.
• Experience within a large global professional services, consulting, shared services or global delivery organization.
• Exposure to enterprise transformation, operating-model change, workforce strategy, technology transformation or large-scale strategic programs.
• Experience working across multiple geographies, functions and senior stakeholder groups.
What We Look For
A seasoned professional who combines the strategic perspective of a Chief of Staff with the execution discipline of a strong PMO leader. The individual should be comfortable operating behind the scenes while having sufficient executive presence to engage senior stakeholders directly. They should be capable of moving from a leadership discussion to a structured set of priorities, from fragmented updates to an enterprise view, and from a complex issue to a clear articulation of what matters, what requires a decision and what needs to happen next.
What Working At EY GDS Offers
EY Global Delivery Services (GDS) is a dynamic global delivery network that works with EY teams across service lines, geographies and sectors. The role offers direct exposure to strategic leadership priorities and the opportunity to strengthen the translation of enterprise strategy into coordinated execution.
EY | Building a better working world 
EY exists to build a better working world, helping to create long-term value for clients, people and society and build trust in the capital markets.
Enabled by data and technology, diverse EY teams in over 150 countries provide trust through assurance and help clients grow, transform and operate.
Working across assurance, consulting, law, strategy, tax and transactions, EY teams ask better questions to find new answers for the complex issues facing our world today.

title: Chief of Staff
description:

title: Chief of Staff and Head of transformation
description:

This role sits at the intersection of corporate strategy, portfolio management, market intelligence, and the CEO and leadership office. You will help answer the most important questions we face where to play, how to win, where to invest, and where to exit or scale. You will bring to that work the same rigour and care that our watchmakers bring to theirs.

• You think strategically and solve problems exceptionally well.

What Makes This Role Different
At Ethos, passion is where it starts and mastery is how you grow. You will sit beside the Managing Director and leadership team on the questions that shape the future of our businesses. The opportunity to learn, travel, work with the finest stakeholders and have real influence to shape the future of the company is what you could look forward to.
WHO SHOULDNT APPLY

Bring your passion. Master your craft.

title: Chief Of Staff
description:
ROLE SUMMARY
The Chief Of Staff – CEO’s Office will work closely with the CEO as a strategic and execution partner, supporting the translation of organizational priorities into actionable plans and measurable outcomes. The role will drive key initiatives from the CEO’s Office end-to-end, including strategic planning, cross-functional programme management, business performance reviews, decision support, market intelligence and follow-through critical priorities.
The incumbent will act as a key liaison between the CEO’s Office and business/functional leaders, ensuring alignment, accountability and timely execution of strategic initiatives, while providing structured insights on business performance, market developments, competition, regulatory trends and emerging opportunities.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Strategic Planning & Execution
• Understand the organisation’s strategic priorities, business model, growth objectives and operating environment.
• Translate the CEO’s strategic priorities into clear initiatives, milestones, ownership and measurable outcomes.
• Drive strategic and cross-functional programmes from conceptualisation through implementation and closure.
• Monitor progress against agreed objectives and proactively highlight risks, dependencies, delays and opportunities.
• Support development of business and functional strategies in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
• Drive structured problem-solving and continuous improvement across strategic initiatives.
CEO Office Programme Management
• Own end-to-end management of key projects, special initiatives and new business opportunities sponsored by the CEO.
• Establish appropriate governance mechanisms to ensure timely implementation and accountability.
• Coordinate across functions to remove execution bottlenecks and ensure alignment on critical priorities.
• Maintain structured tracking of CEO-level commitments, decisions and action items.
• Follow through with respective stakeholders until agreed actions are completed.
Business Performance & Executive Reviews
• Support the CEO in conducting monthly, quarterly and annual business reviews.
• Review key business and financial metrics at agreed frequencies and identify significant trends, deviations and areas requiring management attention.
• Convert business data into concise executive insights and recommended actions.
• Track action items emerging from leadership reviews and ensure timely closure.
• Prepare executive-level presentations, dashboards, briefing notes and decision papers.
Decision Support & Business Analysis
• Conduct structured analysis of strategic proposals, investments, projects and new business initiatives.
• Evaluate the business case, opportunities, risks, dependencies and potential impact of proposed initiatives.
• Synthesize complex information from multiple functions and present clear recommendations to the CEO.
• Support leadership decision-making through data-driven analysis and scenario evaluation.
Market, Industry & Competitive Intelligence
• Track relevant industry, economic, regulatory, customer and competitive developments.
• Analyse market trends, identify emerging opportunities and potential risks, and provide actionable insights to leadership.
• Analyze competitor strategies, products, propositions and market developments.
• Prepare focused reports and recommendations on new markets, products and business opportunities.
• Gather and synthesize information from credible industry reports, publicly available information, field inputs and subscribed/purchased research.
• Engage with relevant customers, partners, professionals and industry bodies, where required, to strengthen market understanding.
Stakeholder Management
• Act as a key coordination point between the CEO’s Office and business/function heads on strategic priorities.
• Build effective working relationships across functions to facilitate faster decision-making and execution.
• Ensure important matters requiring CEO intervention are presented with clear context, supporting analysis and recommended options.
• Handle business-sensitive and confidential matters with appropriate discretion and judgement.
KEY CHALLENGES
• Translating broad CEO priorities into clear, measurable actions across multiple functions.
• Maintaining momentum and accountability across initiatives where ownership sits with different business and functional leaders.
• Balancing urgent executive requests with longer-term strategic priorities.
• Making timely recommendations amid incomplete information, competing priorities and evolving market or regulatory conditions.
• Securing timely cross-functional alignment and support to resolve execution bottlenecks.
KEY DECISIONS TAKEN
• Recommend priorities, sequencing, governance and milestones for CEO-sponsored initiatives.
• Recommend corrective actions or escalation of risks, delays and dependencies affecting strategic delivery.
• Provide analysis and options to support CEO decisions on strategic proposals, investments and business opportunities.
• Recommend actions arising from business performance reviews and executive discussions.
KEY INTERACTIONS
Internal Stakeholders
CEO and CEO’s Office; business and functional heads; Finance; Strategy; Risk; Compliance; Legal; HR; Operations; Technology; Marketing; and other enabling functions, as relevant.
External Stakeholders
Industry and market experts; customers and business partners; consultants/advisors; research providers; industry bodies; and other external stakeholders, as required for strategic analysis and initiatives.
KEY ROLE DIMENSIONS
Scope: Enterprise-wide strategic initiatives and CEO-sponsored programmes
Stakeholder reach: CEO, senior leadership team, business heads and functional leaders
Primary focus: Strategy execution, business performance, decision support and cross-functional coordination
EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE
Minimum Qualification:
• Chartered Accountant (CA) and/or postgraduate qualification in Management/Finance.
• MBA/PGDM from a premier management institution, including IIMs, would be preferred.
Nature of Experience:
• 10–12 years of relevant experience in Strategy, CEO/Chairman/MD Office, Management Consulting, Corporate Planning, Business Finance, Transformation or Programme Management.
• Prior experience working closely with a CEO, Chairman, MD, CXO or senior leadership team will be preferred.
• Experience in BFSI/NBFC/Financial Services would be an advantage.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience developing dashboards, analytical reports and executive presentations.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Us
Chief of Staff to the CEO
Summary
This senior, full-time individual contributor role serves as a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer, operating from Pune with occasional travel to Singapore and key market locations. Designed as a two-to-three-year engagement, the position offers company-wide visibility, collaborating closely with five Product Business Unit (PBU) heads, the CTO organization, and cross-functional leaders in delivery, marketing, finance, and talent. The primary purpose of this role is to establish and maintain a robust operating system that enables the CEO to focus on high-level strategy, capital allocation, and critical personnel decisions. By managing the rhythm of the organization and ensuring seamless execution of cross-unit commitments, the Chief of Staff empowers PBU leaders to drive their respective units effectively while the CEO maintains direct oversight without being bottlenecked by coordination tasks.
Responsibilities
• Orchestrate Operating Rhythms: Manage the end-to-end monthly portfolio review, including agenda setting, standardizing pre-reads, tracking decision logs, and ensuring action items are assigned and completed.
• Develop Outcome Metrics: Create and maintain a unified scorecard for each PBU focusing on business impact, customer satisfaction, and product reliability, collaborating with Finance and Product Marketing to validate data sources.
• Manage Cross-Unit Dependencies: Maintain a central register of customer commitments and shared roadmap items, proactively identifying and resolving conflicts before they impact delivery or client relationships.
• Streamline Executive Decision-Making: Triage and frame all requests requiring CEO attention with clear facts, options, and recommendations, ensuring rapid turnaround times and documenting final decisions for accountability.
• Drive Transformation Execution: Track the implementation of the new PBU operating model, including organizational changes and interim reporting, and prepare strategic reviews with data-driven recommendations for future structural adjustments.
• Facilitate Leadership Alignment: Run the weekly leadership cadence, quarterly business reviews, and annual planning cycles, ensuring high standards for pre-reads, minutes, and action tracking across all forums.
• Monitor Strategic Progress: Partner with the CFO to track company-wide objectives regarding growth, profitability, AI deployment, and market expansion, providing concise monthly updates to the CEO and leadership team.
• Prepare Board and Shareholder Materials: Oversee the quality and timeline of board packs and shareholder reports, ensuring consistency and accuracy in all content derived from functional teams.
• Lead Special Initiatives: Manage time-bound projects scoped by the CEO, such as revenue team reorganizations, new market entry groundwork, and AI strategy rollout, ensuring clear scope, deadlines, and handovers.
• Draft Executive Communications: Author decision memos, briefing notes, and internal communications for the CEO, collaborating with the Content team to ensure external messaging accurately reflects facts and decisions.
• Maintain Local Presence: Act as the daily representative of the CEO office in Pune, providing early insights into unit operations and delivering candid, necessary information to leadership.
Requirements
Requirements:
• Education: An MBA from a top-tier business school (such as an IIM) is required; an undergraduate degree in engineering or a quantitative field is highly preferred.
• Experience: Eight to twelve years of professional experience, including at least three years in a top-tier management consulting firm with a track record of managing engagement managers or equivalent workstreams for C-suite clients.
• Industry Background: Minimum of two years of operational experience within a software, SaaS, or technology product company, specifically in strategy, operations, program management, or a Chief of Staff capacity.
• Proven Track Record: Demonstrated success in leading cross-functional programs to completion within organizations of 200 to 500 employees, with a focus on delivering tangible outcomes rather than just plans.
• Board-Level Competence: Experience in preparing and presenting materials for board-level audiences and working directly with engineering and product leaders to understand the software development lifecycle.
• Core Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, the ability to analyze financial data independently, proficiency in running meetings that result in clear decisions, and the capability to build data-driven scorecards from raw inputs.
• Technical Fluency: Comfortable integrating AI tools into daily workflows and expects similar adoption across teams.
• Working Style: A low-ego professional with a strong commitment to follow-through, capable of delivering difficult truths to senior leadership, and dedicated to seeing problems through to resolution without seeking public credit.
• Location: Must be based in Pune or willing to relocate prior to commencement, with the ability to travel occasionally to Singapore.
Benefits Why Join Anchanto
At Anchanto, we believe in creating an environment where people can build meaningful careers, continuously develop their capabilities and gain exposure to a truly global business.
• Global Exposure: Work with diverse teams, customers and stakeholders across international markets and gain experience in a global B2B SaaS environment.
• Learning & Development: We invest in our people through sponsored learning, certifications and development opportunities aligned with your professional growth.
• International & Onsite Opportunities: Client-facing roles may offer opportunities to travel and work onsite with customers across our global markets.
• Medical Insurance: Comprehensive medical insurance coverage to support you & your family's health and well-being.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Bright Money
Bright Money is a consumer fintech built for middle-income consumers. Our platform helps consumers build credit, manage debt, and access suitable loans and credit cards—addressing the key financial needs of people living paycheck to paycheck.
Bright is a profitable, India-built fintech serving the U.S. market, with a clear trajectory toward $100 million in revenue. Our business model combines subscription revenue with a financial-services marketplace across loans, credit cards, and credit-building solutions.
We have launched an AI-powered money assistant and agentic AI experiences that simplify access to credit. Our ambition is to build the first AI-driven consumer-fintech platform for middle-income consumers.
Founded in 2019, Bright’s founding team includes leaders from McKinsey’s Banking Practice—Petko Plachkov and Avi Patchava—and data science leaders from InMobi. Bright is backed by leading global venture capital firms and technology investors across the U.S., Europe, and Asia.
With a data-driven, high-ownership, and fast-paced culture, we are building a global consumer-fintech company from India.
What is the role about?
We are looking for a Chief of Staff (with a path to Chief Operating Officer) to work directly with Bright’s CEO and leadership team as a strategic partner and force multiplier. You will drive the company’s operating rhythm, translate strategy into execution across functions, and lead the high-priority initiatives that shape Bright’s next phase of growth.
This role is designed as a path to Chief Operating Officer. You will begin by driving strategy and execution alongside the CEO, and progressively take direct ownership of functions, teams, and P&L as you build the operating track record to step into the COO seat.
We are looking for a seasoned operator who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, influences senior stakeholders without formal authority, and is ready to carry line accountability.
What will you do?
• Strategic partnership: Act as a thought partner to the CEO on company strategy, priorities, and key decisions—framing problems, analyzing options, and driving decisions to closure.
• Operating cadence: Own the company’s planning and review rhythm, including annual and quarterly goal-setting, OKRs, business reviews, and leadership meetings, with clear accountability and follow-through.
• Cross-functional execution: Lead high-priority initiatives from scoping through delivery, aligning Product, Engineering, Data Science, Growth, Finance, and Human Potential teams.
• Board & investor readiness: Prepare board decks, investor updates, and leadership communications with Board-level rigor and clarity.
• Performance insight: Track key business metrics and surface risks, bottlenecks, and opportunities early, with data-backed recommendations.
• Special projects: Own strategic projects such as new product or market evaluations, organizational design, and process improvements.
• Leadership leverage: Manage the CEO’s priorities and time, serve as a point of escalation, and represent the CEO in internal and external forums as needed.
• Path to COO: Progressively take direct ownership of functions, operating teams, and P&L, stepping into the Chief Operating Officer mandate as the business scales.
Ideal candidate profile
Experience & Background:
• Experience: 12+ years of professional experience, with a strong foundation in management consulting, investment banking, or strategy and operations roles at high-growth technology companies.
• Leadership exposure: A proven track record of working closely with founders or CXOs; prior experience as a Chief of Staff or in Strategy or BizOps leadership is strongly preferred.
• Domain: Experience in fintech, consumer internet, or financial services is a strong plus; exposure to the U.S. market is an advantage.
• Analytical depth: Strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; comfortable with financial models, business metrics, and data-driven decision-making.
• Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication, including Board-level presentations and executive storytelling.
• Education: Degree from a leading institution; an MBA is preferred.
• Operating scope: Experience owning a function, business line, or P&L, and building and leading teams; the ambition and readiness to step into a COO mandate.
Mindset & Operating DNA:
• Ownership: Treats company outcomes as their own and closes loops without being asked.
• Structured thinking: Brings clarity to ambiguous problems and turns them into actionable plans.
• Bias for action: Moves quickly, prioritizes ruthlessly, and balances speed with rigor.
• Influence without authority: Builds trust across teams and aligns senior stakeholders through credibility rather than hierarchy.
• Discretion & judgment: Handles sensitive information with integrity and makes sound calls under pressure.
• Leadership scale: Ready to move from influence to direct accountability—setting standards, building teams, and owning outcomes end to end.
Non-Fit Profiles
• Profiles focused mainly on executive assistance, scheduling, or administrative support.
• Candidates who prefer advisory work without hands-on ownership of execution and outcomes.
• Those uncomfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, or a fast-paced, high-cadence environment.
• Candidates seeking a long-term staff or advisory seat, with no appetite for line ownership or P&L accountability.
What Bright Offers?
• A profitable sub-unicorn with U.S. market scale – liquidity potential at $1–3B valuations.
• Real ownership: You grow into running your own BU with an independent P&L.
• Wealth creation: Equity at an inflection stage of scale.
• A data-driven, high-cadence culture that combines consulting rigor with FinTech speed.
• Benefits: Excellent benefits package in line with sector best practice.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Artha Group
Artha Group is a performance-first investment house managing ₹2,300 crores across domestic and international investment vehicles, including Category I & II AIFs, LLPs, and Private Limited companies. With active investments in 130+ startups, with 32+ successful exits, and 10+ renewable energy projects. We operate at the convergence of capital precision and operational depth.
Job Title: Chief of Staff to the Managing Partner & CEO
Location: Lower Parel, Mumbai (Onsite, Full-Time)
Role Overview:
Artha is seeking a Chief of Staff to work alongside the Managing Partner & CEO at the center of the firm. This is a senior role with real accountability: for the momentum of the investment lifecycle, the success of the portfolio, the progress of fundraising, and the formation of new funds and entities.
The Chief of Staff sets the firm’s operating cadence and holds it, anticipating what comes next, keeping every priority in motion, and clearing the path when progress slows. Just as importantly, they ensure the Managing Partner’s time, the firm’s scarcest resource, is invested where it matters most.
It is a role built on trust. The Chief of Staff is candid counsel to the Managing Partner, a steadying presence for the team when the stakes are high, and, when the moment calls for it, the firm’s voice in the room.
The role requires:
• Ownership of pace, priorities, and follow-through across the firm
• The foresight to plan two steps ahead
• Judgment on what to escalate and what to resolve
• Executive presence with founders, LPs, and partners
• Composure when the stakes are high
• An independent point of view, and the discipline to execute once a decision is taken
• Discretion beyond question
• The ambition to one day manage a fund
Core Responsibilities
1). Operating Cadence & Execution
• Design and own the firm’s operating cadence: the priorities, forums, and reviews through which the firm moves
• Translate strategic priorities into clear owners, milestones, and timelines
• Work closely with each team to anticipate next steps and keep initiatives on schedule
• Bring rigor to how the firm spends its time, so that every forum earns its place and every commitment made in it is carried through
• Clear bottlenecks early, through direct follow-up and cross-team coordination
2). Investment Lifecycle
• Hold accountability for the momentum of every investment, from first review through Investment Committee, documentation, closing, and post-closing compliance
• Maintain a precise, real-time view of each transaction’s stage, owner, and next step
• Resolve friction in diligence, legal, and approvals before it becomes delay
• Ensure Investment Committee materials are rigorous, timely, and decision-ready
3). Portfolio Success
• Run the portfolio review cadence and hold the firm and its founders to the commitments they make to each other
• Read early signals in performance, governance, and capital needs, and bring them forward while there is still time to act
• Ensure the firm’s value-creation commitments to portfolio companies are delivered
• Keep follow-on, reporting, and exit workstreams on course
4). Fundraising
• Drive the operating rhythm of fundraising: LP pipeline, meeting preparation, and disciplined follow-through
• Ensure data rooms, LP communications, and reporting meet the standard institutional investors expect
• Shape the fundraising calendar around the conversations that matter most
5). Fund & Entity Formation
• Own new fund, SPV, and entity formations from initiation to completion
• Orchestrate legal, tax, compliance, trustee, and regulatory counterparts against the firm’s timelines
• Keep post-formation obligations and governance records in order
6). Amplifying the Managing Partner
• Direct the Managing Partner’s attention to the decisions, relationships, and moments where it creates the greatest value
• Build the team’s judgment on what warrants the Managing Partner’s time and what is best resolved within the firm
• Ensure every engagement arrives with the context, the stakes, and a clear ask
• Continuously refine how time is invested against the value it creates
7). Representation & Relationships
• Represent the firm with founders, LPs, and partners, including in the Managing Partner’s absence where appropriate
• Serve as a trusted counterpart to the team and to the firm’s key relationships
• Know with precision which matters to resolve and which to escalate
• Uphold the highest standards of confidentiality
8). Escalation & Crisis Management
• Lead the firm’s first response when urgent issues arise, whether in the portfolio, with LPs, or on regulatory or reputational matters
• Establish the facts quickly, bring the right people together, and present options with a clear recommendation
• Carry every issue through to resolution
9). Trusted Counsel
• Offer the Managing Partner a candid, independent perspective, particularly when it is least expected
• Stay close to the team and the portfolio, sensing friction and people issues before they surface
• Handle sensitive matters with discretion and maturity
Why This Role
This is neither an executive assistant role nor a coordination function. It offers proximity to the firm’s most significant decisions and exposure across the full life of a fund: investing, portfolio, fundraising, and formation. Responsibility grows with performance.
For those who aspire to manage a fund, there are few better places to learn how one is built and run.
Must-Have Qualifications
• 5–10 years of experience in venture capital, private equity, investment banking, consulting, or a high-growth environment
• Working knowledge of the investment lifecycle, fund structures, and fund operations
• A record of leading cross-functional initiatives to completion
• Strong financial and commercial acumen
• Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication
• Experience working directly with founders, Managing Partners, or CXOs
• MBA or equivalent from a top-tier institution preferred
Traits That Matter
• Ambition to build a career in fund management
• An instinct for pace and an insistence on follow-through
• High agency and a deep sense of ownership
• Structured thinking that turns ambiguity into clear plans
• Composure under pressure
• Loyalty paired with independent judgment
• Executive presence
• Discretion and integrity
Compensation
• Fixed Annual Salary: Rs. 32,00,000,
• Fixed Retention Bonus: Rs. 3,00,000, paid at the end of each year
• ESOP Eligibility: Rs. 2,50,000, vesting as per policy
• Total Annual Compensation: Rs. 37,50,000

The Project/Program Manager plays a critical role in driving strategic and operational initiatives for the Global Capability Center (GCC). title: Chief of Staff
description:
JOIN OUR COMPANY
• We are inviting applicants for our chief of staff program. We’re looking for high energy, talented colleagues who enjoy the collaborative, fast paced and innovative culture of a high growth company. And are hungry for an opportunity to grow with the team and have a lot of fun learning along the way.
• We believe there is a real gap in the retail market for healthy food and snacks for children and adults. And if you care passionately about this, then join us to make this better!
• If you’re a pro-active someone who enjoys getting things done in an entrepreneurial set up, then read on!
WHAT WE DO AND WHO WE ARE
Please do take a look at our website www.slurrpfarm.com and www.livemille.com where you will find more information on both of our brands
Slurrp Farm is a food brand for parents who are looking to give their child a healthy start to life and Mille is a brand for adults looking for high protein, high fiber and delicious functional food. We believe that, in many ways, we need to go back to eating like our grandparents did; to the nutritious traditional food that has existed for millennia in India. Thanks to the invaluable support of experts in food and nutrition, we help parents fighting the good fight of feeding their children healthy from an early age and making it fun. And we help families across India and the world, make better choices for themselves. Our mission is to “Change the Way the World Eats. One plate at a time”
The founders of Slurrp Farm, Shauravi Malik and Meghana Narayan, are foodies, entrepreneurs and parents to young children.
• Meghana used to run the public health practice at McKinsey India, and has studied at Harvard Business School, was a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford University and a Computer Science engineer from Bangalore University. She was also on the Indian national swimming team and it is her personal goal to up the nutrition table for Indian kids. 
• Shauravi used to work for Sir Richard Branson's Group Holding entity at the Virgin Group, and in the Consumer and Healthcare Investment Banking team at JP Morgan in London. She studied Economics at Cambridge University and at St. Stephen's College in Delhi University. 
WHAT WILL BE YOUR MISSION IN THE CHIEF OF STAFF PROGRAMME?
This role sits right at the heart of Wholsum Foods. Over 12–24 months, you will work directly with the two co-founders in helping the company to achieve its strategic and operational goals. The Chief of Staff Career Program moves you across functions and cross-functional projects, working directly with ExCo leaders from across the business. It gives you a real time view of how a company really works that very few roles offer, early in a career. Your mission is to learn how the business grows and steadily becoming ready for larger roles in our organization, or on to the next step in your career and education.
OUTCOMES: WHAT ARE YOU GOING TO DO IN THE PROGRAMME?
Across the program, you'll take on a mix of short, fast-turnaround assignments and longer pieces of work you really get to own, drive and impact WF. As an example, one candidate's path might start in Finance: a profitability review, maybe a feasibility study for a new product line, which has a direct impact on Operations function. Before moving into another assignment in Finance or taking on a Brand campaign or a process efficiency study. From there, it might lead into the Online business, co-owning a channel rollout or digging into pricing and margins, and later, a process redesign taken end-to-end or a cross-functional product launch led start to finish. The role will take shape around business needs and where your own interests lead.
WHAT VALUES DO WE LOOK FOR?
Growth Mindset
Dependable
Relationship First
Passionate
OTHER QUESTIONS
1. What will you think about (a lot of the time?)
• Am I pushing the co-founders to become better at what they do, every day?
• Am I living the company values, and working in sync with them, to the best of my ability? 
• Am I excited to be part of this program, because I can see myself becoming the best version of me?
2. Why is this exciting to you?
If you can work with ambiguity and thrive in creating systems and structures around it, enjoy solving complex problems, and are ready to work at the pace of a fast-scaling company, this role gives you the space to do all these.
• You are interested to operationalize strategy in a real world setting
• You are keenly interested in the digital space in India, and interested in FMCG food businesses
• You are interested in learning how to build great workplaces within a company that is both growing and highly diverse
• You are about people, you care about being invested in, as an individual and you believe in mentorship
• We are laying the foundation of a culture of conscious capitalism and this is your chance to work somewhere that enables you to road test a shared passion
• After the CEO office role for 2-3 years you will either - a) run a large department that you enjoyed working in at Slurrp Farm b) do this at another corporate or c) venture into the world of operating companies at a PE/VC fund or d) go do your MBA or further studies
3. Where have you been?
• You will have 3-5 years of prior work experience
• You love owning something end-to-end — whether that's a project or program, a strategy or business-analyst role with real delivery accountability, or an operations process that was truly yours to run.
• You're genuinely curious about how the business works, and you love learning - Business Understanding and Continuous Learning are the two things we'll get to know through conversation with you.
• Real, on-the-ground experience of working in India is something we genuinely value in your background.
LOCATION
Gurgaon, India

Channel Partner Management
• Design and execute a channel strategy that delivers the required market coverage, capability, service levels, compliance and commercial performance.

• Categorize KOLs by specialty, institution, geography, clinical influence, academic contribution, and portfolio relevance.
